 The pattern of organization is not always clear, and sometimes it seems like a typescript of note cards; however, some interesting points are made along the way. Among others that the look of the consumptive became a fashionable look, a look to be acquired by the social class climber, and a look behind the [still] current fascination with thinness. The few social class and economic analyses were very interesting. 
 It is instructive to follow the shifts as TB/consumption's myths split, the romanticized going to mental illness and the negative going to cancer. 
 Worth having read. And the introduction of an idea can be forgiven for absence of enough analysis. More analysis will be good, and I am sure someone will do/has done it.

This novel, more character study than action based, begins well. There is enough foreshadowing in the opening to grab reader attention, and the characters quickly become likeable. I enjoyed following their ups and downs and inabilities to communicate for the first two thirds. Then it got a little old. The author seemed to realize that possibility and did a lot of summary narrative in the last third, but it was still hard to finish. I had anticipated how each would end. I like to be a little bit surprised. 
 At one point Reiko narrates a situation with a piano student. On first reading, I did not see where it was necessary to the plot or the reading experience. I may be more observant if I read the novel again, which I will not be rushing to do.
I might have liked it better if I had read it closer to when it was written. I did learn something about ocean currents and ice ages, though, and got references to learn more.

Kingsolver adroitly addresses climate change via a fictitious change in the migration pattern of monarch butterflies. For the most part the information comes in a way appropriate to characters and their interest; occasionally when it was something familiar to me, it got tedious, but usually it remained interesting. 
 Delarobia, the narrator, became increasingly interesting as a character as the novel progressed. Characters unlikeable at the beginning gradually became likeable. Changes were adequately motivated. The ending was believable. 
 There was some wonderful humor in the mixing of cultures through characters' interaction: scientific with non-scientific, Appalachian with outsider.
Spell binding pageturner.

This is the first Erdrich novel told from one character's point of view throughout that I have read, and it is well done. Erdrich uses a few sneaky ways to get other peoples' information into the story, but they are believable (even the dream stories). I was glad to see familiar names. Nanapush has a significant role, and others make a cameo appearance (Father Damien, a character from The Bingo Palace, and two other families whose names I recognized but can't think of now). 
 There is an interesting balance between the tense plot moments and boyish day-to-day moments as the plot moves inevitably onward to a satisfying ending. We really get to know the major characters, and I found most quite likeable.

I am glad I read the book before any of the reviews--many not labeled spoilers are indeed spoilers. 
 The novel has many strengths. The plotting and pacing for one. I like a novel that switches between past and present so long as I know where I am, and this one succeeds there. In addition after half way through, I could not put it down. I anticipated many details before they were revealed, but I realized them gradually, and knowing did not spoil anything for me because there was always something else that was not so apparent to read for. I am intrigued by all the people who liked the beginning and not the ending; for me it was the opposite. 
 Mason, Irene, Bliss, Jeff were the more developed and more likeable characters. In contrast to those who found Pastor White one-dimensional and stereotypical, I found him believable--I have known Christians who are that rigid and rule bound--and rounded by the tornado scenes where he cared for the migrants immediate needs by providing shelter and for their long range needs by finding alternate work for them and helping them with transportation to it. And since we are all bundles of contradictions, I could believe both features coexisted in one man. 
 The weaknesses for me included too many sub stories, an unrealistically prolonged grieving period (though the depth of grief was realistic), and an unlikely romance. 
 ETA I'm revising my opinion about the unrealistically prolonged grieving. It was my first reaction because I've know people in deep grief who did not spiral downward like Irene did. The revision has two sources. The depth was needed to balance what happened next. And having heard Rakha talk about two real life situations where a victim's family member grieved for 12+ years expanded my sense of possibility.

As with all historic fiction, the more one knows about the period, the richer the read. And when I don't know, I am prompted to learn the history. This novel is set during Argentina's military dictatorship, 1976-1984 or so, a time of repression, witch hunts, and people disappearing. 
 Distance is created by two things: The perspective is of an elder, reflecting on life, on past actions, philosophizing. And often the narration slips into the voice of a ten-year-old boy who is somewhat removed from politics by his age, though he hears and reports enough for readers to understand. He is also wise and witty; he and his five-year-old brother cook up some entertaining episodes. 
 Generally the philosophizing fits right in and is unobtrusive. However, near the end there are three short chapters that feel more like essays than story. That is the only flaw I've found with the book. I especially appreciated musings on memory and time, like this one:"Sometimes there are variations in what I remember. . . . These variations . . . mean I'm remembering something I hadn't noticed before; they mean I'm not exactly the same person I was when last I remembered" (5).

Although I resent books that merely capitalize on classics (the ...and zombie variety), I value books that attempt to show the fictive world from the perspective of the victimized when what we had before was the version of the victor (the retelling of Beowulf as Grendal's Dam for example). 
 Wide Sargasso Sea falls into the latter group. Jean Rhys writes what might have been the story of the mad woman, Bertha, in the attic of Jane Eyre. I had read it once before, but my reading of Jane Eyre was very distant; this time it was recent and in some ways filled in gaps as this book filled in gaps in the earlier work, expanding the time Rochester was in the West Indies, betrayed by his family into a marriage for money. 
 The point of view shifts are handled well in parts 1 and 3, but are signaled too far into the changes in part 2; still the shifts have value. By shifting the narration from Antoinette (later to be named Bertha by Rochester, called Bertha Antoinette Mason in Jane Eyre) to Rochester Rhys gives us two perspectives on Jamaican life. Antoinette, a white Creole, an outsider to the black Jamaicans, though puzzled by the attitude of the ex-slaves, is more of the culture. Rochester's middle portion shows him as totally outsider, uncomprehending. 
 Various versions are told, and at this read I have not resolved if any is meant to be "the" truth. Although there is madness in Antoinette's family history, there is some possibility of it having been caused by external circumstances, likewise with her madness in part three. Regardless of which version is given credence, the Antoinette/Bertha character draws more sympathy. 
 It is a short, but rich, novel. Valuable in itself, but also a valuable expansion beyond the European version.
Deeply troubling. Deeply moving. Moves inexorably to its end.

This amazing book caught my interest with the first paragraph, and that without the 'in medias res' beginning. Oh there was back story, but the actual plot began in Chapter 1 with two girls stealing fruit. 
 The pace is leisurely for the first two thirds, then speeds up, the style descriptive and immediate. There were few characters, though towns and other activities were implied. The characters were well developed with flaws and virtues--all but one, who had no redeeming qualities. 
 Much of the book was about ideas never stated (the Orchardist himself, Jane and Della, sometimes Caroline Middey, though she was the most likely to speak) or about inability to speak (Clee). Angeline was more the one who wanted to know than one not communicating. Each had their own type of isolation, though there were also relationships. 
 The novel deals with aging, birth, the growing up of children, and the diminished abilities of the elderly, always matter of factly, sometimes understated. Never heavy handed philosophizing. 
 This is a rare book that remains excellent through the ending. No strong woman is forced to marry. The orchard doesn't last forever.

Written as a collection of graphic essays by various authors/artists. Thus it is not a chronological history. There is repetition (not a bad thing...events reappear with variations in different contexts) and mixed quality. Some of the art work adds great meaning to the text. A good introduction.

** spoiler alert ** 
 Generally, I like the slow pace of 19C novels, the extended description of setting and person. I like getting drawn into the fictitious world. I like the battles of wits and psychological studies. And this novel has those. 
 I like that the novel is narrated as if it were a memoir, written (we learn at the end) ten years after most events. 
 I dislike the hints of Beauty and the Beast mythology in Jane and Rochester. Yes, he does get tamed and become likeable; but I get tired of seeing women put into the civilizing role. 
 I tolerated the moralizing via various characters as part of 19C until we came to St John. He was just too preachy and went on way too long. At first I shrugged it off as part of his character, and I hypothesized that Bronte was mocking him in presenting it to excess, especially when he claims that he has God's will for someone else, for Jane, who had no such internal push to become a missionary. Then I came to the ending of the novel and wondered why it ended with him, his anticipation of death told in Revelation terms. Was this meant to elevate him? To make this the lesson for all from the novel? Was it meant to say he had never changed? That it did say, but why end thus? Is even the end part of the mockery of his approach to life--mocking importance to a self important man? 
 Another place that did not work for me was Rochester's narration of his past to Jane after the wedding has been called off. Mere telling went on way too long. 
 I also could not believe that the feisty Jane could be almost persuaded by St John. Yes Bronte did try to make it believable by Jane's saying that she was docile and obedient until a certain level of resistance had been reached and then she would fight back. And as a child she had been excessively obedient, but then she had grown out of it. So I wasn't convinced that she remained in character. Of course, her being almost persuaded did add to the drama. It would have done so more had it been believable. 
 In spite of features, which to me seemed faults, overall it was a good read.

This book laughed me to tears many times. It's does a great job at calling into question the reality of the situation people are put in on a day-to-day basis. I recommend reading this book to anyone that has the time. It is long and should probably be read when you don't have too many distractions around you.

Rowling knows how to paint human beings, but unlike her characters in Harry Potter who demonstrate the power of love and heroism, the characters in Casual Vacancy demonstrate all the selfish and entitled attitudes of the human race. The book is worth reading as long as you are able to separate reality from fantasy acknowledge the horrors of our fleshly desires.

I really don't know what to say about this book that would do it any justice. It is beautifully written, and addresses questions that every person, regardless of age or religious belief has to struggle with at some point in his or her life. 
 Just to give anyone a reference on whether or not you will like this book if you read it: 
 If you liked the coming of age novel, The Catcher in the Rye, by J.D. Salinger, then you will love this novel. It is also a coming of age novel that as adapted for this day and age. If you hated The Catcher in the Rye, like I did, then you will also love this novel because it succeeds at everything plus some that The Catcher in the Rye did not. I highly recommend this book.
I liked it! There were slow parts, and it is a rather depressing book, but McCourt does a wonderful drop at lightening the mood.

Quindlen does a great job at describing the thoughts and emotions that victims of domestic abuse experience. With that said, I felt that this book began strong but ended rather one-dimensional, with little else to take from it. Good book for a fast read.

The writing was superb. It's a great commentary on the Dresden bombings during WWII and on the destruction of war in general. While I found the narrative itself pretty boring, I found Vonnegut's ability to portray postmodern concepts through his style very interesting. I would recommend this book for anyone. Even if it's not your cup of tea, it is an American classic that everyone should be familiar with.

Chuyen phieu luu cua Zazie bat dau o ga Austerlitz, khi me dua em len Paris gui o nha cau Garbiel de ba du hi cung tinh nhan. Kinh do anh sang qua lang kinh cua co be muoi ba tuoi rat la lung: Hoigimahoithe, thien duong khong phai la nhung cung dien trang le, thap Eiffel hay toa Pantheon ma la tau dien ngam. Khi he thong tau dien ngam ngung hoat dong do dinh cong, Zazie quyet dinh tu kham pha Paris theo cach rieng minh. 
 Suyt tro thanh nan nhan tinh duc cua cha ruot va bo duong, da ra toa lam chung de cuu me, chung kien me chay theo cac nhan tinh mot cach tuyet vong... Zazie va ngon ngu cua minh gia dan hon tuoi muoi ba nhieu. Hien nhien, su bo ba va nguoc ngao cua Zazie da gay ra khong it rac roi cho Gabriel va nhung nguoi trong khu nha La Cave. Nhung thac mac hon nhien thang than cua Zazie da khien nhung nguoi lon xung quanh "chong ca mat" va hanh dong bat ngo: Tai xe taxi Charles vuot qua noi so de hoi cuoi nguoi tinh con vu cong Gabriel thi ven tam voan kin dao ve "hoat dong nghe thuat" cua minh cho ban be chiem nguong... 
 Nhung tinh huong cua "Zazie trong tau dien ngam" duoc xay dung kha chat che voi nhieu nut that-mo. Su thong minh, quyet doan da giup Zazie vuot qua nhung kho khan bat ngo khi phai ung pho mot minh. Hanh trinh cua Zazie duoc mo ta hap dan theo cau truc mot bo phim hai hanh dong: Bang su trong treo va ca tinh phong khoang, Zazie da duong dau voi the gioi nguoi lon, chong lai lop vo ngot ngao gia tao cua ho, va nhan duoc loi thu thi cay dang: "Hay cam thong voi nguoi lon".... 
 Thong qua cac rac roi cua Zazie, nguoi doc cung thay duoc boi canh nuoc Phap nhung nam 60's, cam nhan Paris voi du mang sang - toi chu khong chi la thien duong hoa le. Diem thu vi la ngay ca khi ke ve nhung dieu xam xit cua cuoc song, Raymond Queneau cung khien ta bat cuoi vi cach su dung tu ngu hom hinh. Day cung la tac pham thoi lan gio moi vao van hoc Phap kinh dien boi nhung pha cach ky cong trong viec su dung tu ngu "via he". Von noi tieng voi viec sang tao cac kieu viet moi, Queneau da kheo leo su dung cac tieng long duong pho vua gan gui voi tang lop binh dan, song cung khong qua tho tuc voi nhung nguoi doc quen ngon tu chin chu. Voi sang tao cac nhan vat la thuong, ong da ve ra buc tranh tong hop chan dung nhung nguoi-lon-dac-trung thoi bay gio mot cach hai huoc, kem theo nhung man doi thoai an tuong. Su ky cong va tinh nhan van cua tac gia da bien cau chuyen cua Zazie - von buon ba, tro thanh cau chuyen lap lanh hi vong ve su thay doi nhung dieu xam xit tuong chung da "bam re" trong cuoc song cua nhung nguoi lon. 
 Zazie da kham pha ra nhieu dieu o Paris hon la tau dien ngam nhu ban dau co be ao uoc. Zazie don nhan nhung bat cap cua xa hoi duong dai mot cach than nhien den hon nhien. "Con gia di" - cau tra loi cua Zazie khi me hoi ve nhung viec da lam o Paris khien nguoi doc sung sot va buon thap thoang. Nhung dua tre truong thanh khi di qua giac mo cua chung luc nao khong hay, giong nhu Zazie cuoi cung da duoc di tau dien ngam ma khong he biet do da thiep di truoc do. Do co le la mot ket thuc la lung nhung hop ly cho mot tac pham tuyet voi.

Truoc gio toi khong thich dan ong viet tan man nhieu, co gi do hoi vun vat. Toi cang khong thich nhung nguoi qua tu tin o ban than minh trong cach the hien cau chu cung nhu chung to su thong minh khi thau tom tam ly nguoi doc bang su don ep cua ngu nghia. La khong thich, the thoi! 
 "Thoi tiet do thi" duoc the hien boi mot giong van tinh cua mot cai dau lanh va tham tram. Nam bat duoc tam ly nguoi doc, tac gia rat kheo leo trong viec the hien tu duy logic va cam tinh vua phai trong nhung trang viet. Cuon sach duoc bien tap tot voi nam phan Life (Song) - Stories (Truyen) - Review (Diem phim, sach, nhac) - Artists (Van nghe sy) - Think Different (Nghi khac) bao quat kha nhieu van de trong nhung nam gan day. Co le day la uu diem cua cuon sach tong hop, nhat la khi no xuat phat tu mot blogger lang thang giang ho mang lau nam. Nguoi doc kho tinh den dau cung se tim duoc mot entry phu hop voi linh vuc minh quan tam. Chua han da thich, nhung it ra co the doc trong nhung luc ranh roi, va ban tan trong luc tra du tuu hau voi ban be. 
 Nhung thay doi duong nhien cua con nguoi va xa hoi trong "Thoi tiet do thi" ta co the chung kien hang ngay o bat cu dau. Nhieu den muc nguoi ta quen ca cam giac nen buon cho cai thoi the ay, nen tiec cho con nguoi va cai cam giac xua cu ay. Va "khi nguoi ta thoi tre", nguoi ta cang biet cach "hoa vang" cam xuc bang chiec ao ngon tu khach quan. Lan khuat dau do trong nhung trang viet la niem tin mat mat, su chua xot va mot noi buon trong treo. Giong nhu tac gia vua tan ra mot giac mo dai tham tham... 
 ... 
 Toi nay toi xem mot buoi dien tai quan cafe quen. Xen giua nhung bai hat la mot minishow standup comedy cua mot nhan vat dao nay dang noi. Bo qua y kien chu quan cua toi, thi feedback cua doc gia sau khi nghe + xem vo hai kich tu bien tu dien cua dong chi nay da khien cho ban toi - tuc la chu quan dau dau trong viec co tiep tuc moi dong chi nay o lai dien nua hay khong. Nguoi che va khen ngang nhau, ma ben nao cung kich liet ly luan. Ben khen thi keu la moi la, ma phan anh dung dan voi nhung gi nghe, thay hang ngay. Ben che thi bao "vua tuc vua tom", nhung chuyen trong wc hay giuong chieu cung dem ra talk o trong khung canh lang man diu dat nua chu, co la comedy chang nua thi cung phan cam. Dieu thu vi la nhung nguoi ung ho Mr.D trong buoi toi hom nay phan lon la chi em phu nu. Tu nhien thay co vai diem tuong dong voi cuon sach nay. Nua dem tac luoi nghi co khi nao de doc gia hay nhung nha phe binh bot dau dau ma da loai bot su du doi di chang? Dau sao gai ham mo da (van) hom hom roi, can chi nua nhung du luan trai chieu?

Nhung nam cuoi doi, Lev Tolstoy da roi bo cuoc song cua mot dai Ba Tuoc giau co day danh vong, chuyen ra o mot minh trong thai ap nho vung nong thon va song nhu nguoi hanh huong ngheo kho nhat. Trong buc thu dai viet cho vo khuoc tu su tro ve, ong noi "...su tro ve cua toi bay gio hoan toan khong the duoc nua...Cuoc song khong phai la tro dua, chung ta khong co quyen tu y vut bo no di va do no theo chieu dai thoi gian cung khong hop ly. Co the la nhung thang cuoi cung trong doi chung ta lai quan trong hon tat ca nhung nam da qua va phai song nhung thang cuoi cung do cho tot dep...". Tai nha ga xep mien Trung Nga, vao mot dem lanh gia thang 11 ong da thuc hien cuoc dao thoat cuoi cung trong cong cuoc tim kiem loi dap cho cac cau hoi giay vo ong suot nhung nam cuoi cua cuoc doi. 
 Chac gi nhung cau tra loi da de chiu hon cau hoi? Dieu nay chi minh Lev Tolstoy biet. Su dan vat trong qua trinh di tim chuoi nhung cau tra loi cho cuoc doi minh duoc ong bieu dat day cay dang va chan thuc trong "Tu thu". Tan bi kich cua mot tam hon manh me va tham thuy, day sang tao va chan chuong, vua phan dau tien toi su tu hoan thien (self - perfection) vua ngap tran su nghi ngai hoang mang... 
 Ngay phan mo dau, ta co the duoc su xung dot manh me giua Duc tin va Ly tri trong con nguoi ong. Tiep sau "Mot tranh luan ve duc tin tai Kremli" va "Nhung nguoi dam thoai" (The Interculor) - ma ong dua ra nhung thao luan ve duc tin giua nhung ke co duc tin va nhung ke vo than, toi "Tu thu" ong da tien mot buoc dai hon han. Ay la phu dinh hoan toan Duc Tin, bang nhung tu ngu danh thep, nhung mau chuyen gian di nhung chac nich da gat bo hoan toan nhung giao ly Chinh thong duoc truyen day tu thoi au tho va khang dinh cai noi chon ma ong von nghi la chua dung Duc tin ay thuc ra da trong rong tu lau va nhung cu chi hanh le hoan toan la vo nghia. Chinh su xung dot manh me giua Duc tin va Ly tri trong con su tu cua van hoc Nga da khien ong bi giao hoi Nga khai tru va coi nhu "mot ke ta dao, xac xuoc va noi loan chong lai Duc chua troi" (ngay 22 thang 2 nam 1901). 
 Va cho den cuoi doi, hanh dong roi bo to am quy toc cua ong cung duoc coi nhu mot hanh vi noi loan, canh sat da bam sat ong, bao chi xon xao, chinh quyen luon san sang doi pho va Nga hoang da cu Toa thanh giao chu Parpheni toi gap ong yeu cau ong hoa giai voi Chinh giao nhung that bai. Cau hoi ve Duc Tin, ve moi quan he giua con nguoi voi dang vo han, y nghia cuoc song cua chinh minh khong ngung am anh Lev Tolstoy va tiep tuc the hien su giang co o doan cuoi tac pham. Rot cuoc, ngon lua thuc su cua Duc Tin nam o dau? O Thuong De vo han hay o trong chinh moi con nguoi? Lev Tolstoy khao khat di tim mot cuoc song co Duc Tin, mot Duc Tin thuan khiet, khong vu loi, mot Duc Tin tu minh tim thay, de co the tu tra loi phan nao cau hoi can thiet phai dat ra. Va ong da tim cho toi tan giay phut cuoi cung cua cuoc doi... 
 Loi thu toi thu nhat: toi chua bao gio co niem tin vao ton giao mot cach nghiem tuc 
 Loi thu toi thu hai: toi da song nhu mot nguoi dien suot nhung nam thang tuoi tre. 
 "Bay gio thi toi thay ro rang khong co su khac biet nao giua chung toi va nhung nguoi (dien) dang song trong mot nha thuong dien; vao thoi ay, toi chi mo ho thoang thay dieu nay, va, giong nhu tat ca moi nguoi dien, toi nghi rang tru toi ra, tat ca nhung nguoi khac deu dien ca." 
 Lev Tolstoy goi nhung nam thang song khat khao cong hien cho dam me quyen luc, danh vong, su giau co, tinh kieu ngao, su dam dang va tham chi la ca khoang thoi gian ben gia dinh..., la nhung nam thang dien ro va doi tra. (Du trong nhung nam nay ong da cho ra doi nhung tac pham duoc coi la kiet tac nhu Chien tranh & hoa binh, Anna Karenina...). 
 Cho den khi ong phat hien ra ong bi "benh", va nhung cau hoi quay ve giang xe dau oc ong. Phai chang tat ca su giau sang va danh vong kia chi la nhung ao anh lua doi cua cuoc doi, va rang suot nhung nam qua ong khong thuc su co uoc vong gi? 
 Loi thu toi thu ba... 
 Loi thu toi thu tu... 
 Loi thu toi thu nam... 
 Xung dot dien ra lien tiep, nhung cau hoi nhay mua, nhung gia dinh khap khoi cuoi noi, cac bac hien nhan nhu Socrates, Solomon, Schopenhauer cung tham chien. Va ket qua la "thay vi mot cau tra loi, tat ca nhung gi ma nguoi ta co the dat toi, la chinh cac cau hoi tuong tu, duoc dat ra trong mot hinh thuc roi ram phuc tap." Giong nhu mot ke bi lac trong rung, mot lan nua, Lev Tolstoy cay dang nhan ra "Toi da khong the bi danh lua. Moi su deu la hu vo, Hanh phuc thay cho ke nao chua tung duoc sinh ra; cai chet thi tot hon cuoc song; chung ta phai loai bo su song ra khoi chinh minh."

Giac mo My" - lan dau tien toi nghe cum tu nay la khi doc "Gatsby vi dai", khi do goi y nghia tuoi sang. Con khi doc cuon "Tren duong" cua Jack Kerouac, cam giac ay hoan toan tan vo. Hien nhien, cuon sach ra doi khi giac mo My da tan vo. Tiep noi "the he bo di" (The Lost Generation) cua Ernest Hemingway hay F. Scott Fitzgerald la "the he Beat" (The Beat Generation) cua Jack Kerouac voi nhung nhip dap ngam trong long nuoc My ngap ngua jazz, sex, ma tuy, su bi an, nhung con duong rong mo day khat khao tu do, nhung con nguoi sinh ra da vo mong: Su giau co khong lam ho an tuong, ho khong biet minh dang tim kiem noi nao de nuong tua, nhung van khong ngung kiem tim 
 "Tren duong" - cuon sach tran day cam hung cho nhung tam hon khat chay tu do, say me nhung chuyen di dai, ham muon trai minh khap moi mien. No khien ban san sang bo lai tat ca va len duong. Cuoc phieu luu xuyen nuoc My cua doi ban than trong truyen duoc coi la lay nguyen mau tu chinh tac gia Jack Kerouac va nguoi ban than cua ong - nha tho Neal Cassady - ma ve thuc chat chuyen di ay la de tim kiem y nghia va su trai nghiem dich thuc trong moi cuoc song. Doi ban than nay (ca trong sach lan ngoai doi) deu khien khong it nguoi vua yeu vua ghet, vua ganh ty lan than phuc boi tu tuong tu do va la lung, chinh ho va tac pham cua ho da tao cam hung cho rat nhieu the he nha van, nhac si, nha tho sang tac. 
 Man phep bo qua nhung linh vuc khac, chi xin nhac toi Rock thi Jack Kerouac va Neal Cassady cung la khoi nguon cho rat nhieu sang tac cua nhung nhac gao coi nhu King Crimson hay Grateful Dead. O Album Beat (King Crimson), diem nhan cua album la ca khuc Neal and Jack and me voi nhieu tiet tau la day cam hung pha tron jazz vao Prog rock va su dung nhieu nhac cu moi khien nguoi nghe vo cung thich thu. Hay trong bai The Other One cua Grateful Dead da tung nhac toi Neal voi hinh anh Cowboy Neal : 
 "The bus came by and I got on, that's when it all began 
 There was Cowboy Neal at the wheel of the bus to Nevereverland". 
 Thuc su, doi voi nhung nguoi thich nhung chuyen di, thi cam giac khi dang "tren duong" la thich thu hon rat nhieu doi voi "dich den". Tham chi, co doi khi cham chan vao "diem den" roi lai thay nhu minh da mat mat di mot thu gi do rat lon lao. Ay la mot doan ket buon. Co le boi vay ma nhung cuoc hanh trinh cu the tiep dien, khong the ngung lai duoc, ca trong cuon sach nay lan o ngoai doi thuc. Toi biet chu, cai cam quan buon ba khi ngay mot tien gan hon toi diem den ma minh dinh truoc, cai khoanh khac ma nhung con duong minh di qua mo dan di, roi cuoc hanh trinh dung lai. Roi, no giong nhu la minh dang di lac trong suong mu. Co doi lan khi nhung chuyen di dai sap ket thuc, toi cam nhan sau sac rang minh da danh mat mot dieu gi do rat quan trong.Thi thoang toi khong xac dinh noi minh dang di tim dieu gi qua nhung chuyen di khi ma tro ve cu khong nguoi buon ba. U, mot doan ngat lung lung u buon, chi la nhung quang nghi giua nhung chuyen di thoi ma! Toi khong biet co luc nao dung lai duoc khong, nhung ke hoach va chuyen di ay - no cu dai dan ra nhanh hon la toc moc. Moi lan nhu the, toi deu nho toi cuon sach nay cung cai ket cung buon ba khong kem ay. Thuc ra, chi la mot hinh anh nguoi o lai, va mot nguoi khac tiep tuc cuoc hanh trinh thoi, vay ma sao buon den the?

I fell in love with this story very quickly. It does take a few chapters to get going, but once it does, it captivates you. You fall into this world of dragons, magic, and sword play. You follow a young boy as he discovers who and what he is. Throughout the four books you watch Eragon, along with Sephira, learn and grow. I truly wish and believe that this book should be required reading for students. Not only would they enjoy it and actually read it, they may even learn something. Christopher Paolini gave us a wonderful look in to his amazing mind. I loved it so much that i bought all the books for myself and my husband for Christmas this year. I believe every one should read this book, along with their children. You will fall in love and want to read it over and over.

I've had this book for quite sometime but I've never dared reading it. Maybe I just felt like it's gonna be another lame story but I was completely wrong. Nothing about this book made me giggle or cry, there was no extreme emotion exerted. But what makes this book special to me is that, it came from a boy's perspective. I've never read a book that has been published, complete and is not a sequel or telling his part of the story after a girl just said her part. It's completely his story, his perspective. And I was overwhelmed. 
 I love the simplicity of the story. There's a lot of firsts in this book. First time to read a book from a boy's perspective, first time read a book that talks about war, first time to read a book that is almost towards the steamy part but just instantly drops it off and move on to the next scene... And I love firsts. 
 I love how Travis was so hard to his mom but eventually he became soft and tried to be the son that he has deprived of his mom. I love how he has such a big heart to help other people. I mean it reminded me of lessons we have in Dev Comm. He'd rather give his money to charity than to spend it on him. 
 I wish Trish Doller just experimented more and explored other possibilities. But over-all, I love its simplicity and staight forwardness.

There are two stories on this book. The first one, well IT WAS BORING and you don't know where the story is heading. I mean Seriously? Based on the title, I kept predicting what could be the reason behind the title... When a situation lead to the title, it's frustrating how the author just instantly dropped off the scene and continue on as if it doesn't matter. Reading through it, it was just one of the typical stories you'll read. I even infact loved the part where Alex writes about her delusions, it was good though.

This book gave a new twist on the epic "I hate him!" turned "I love him!" stories. Who would have thought that it's possible for you to like someone for more than a decade already... Who would have thought that it's possible for you to love the guy whom you got to know as a person who's sex mad and insatiable but the truth is he's none of those... Who would have thought that for 8 years they've got to sleep in one bed every night and whenever they're not together, they couldn't sleep well or either of them will have nightmares... And who would have thought despite all of the bad records done in the past, you can still be madly in love with that person. 
 Indeed, the book proves that once you're in love with someone he's past becomes frivolous and meaningless. Although you'll have some apprehensions but it still boils down to the love you feel for the person. 
 I love the simplicity of the story and how the author wrote about Liam's perspective. I love how the characters grew and the transition to one story to another was seamless and discernible. 
 I wish to have someone like Liam. He's sweet, patient, respectful, funny, protective and sincere. 
 I wish to have someone like Jake. I want to have a brother who looks after his little sister, a brother who will kick everyone's ass once he knows that his little sister is hurt, a brother who loves you unconditionally and is willing to risk his own life just to protect you. 
 Although there were a lot of grammatical errors but I'd like to not dwell on it because the story itself is too beautiful to concentrate on its errors. 
 It's worth reading!

Everything was wrapped in one book. It seems like Molly McAdams doesn't want to have a sequel or something. She squeezed in all the possibilities which makes the book a little boring towards the end of the story. Although it was nice but things were kinda melodramatic, too forgiving, too kind, too accepting, too fast.... 
 Well, Harper is one hell of a girl! She just got into a new world and she just barely set foot on that new world and she immediately met a guy who likes her and make out with him, another guy who's madly in love with her but pisses her all the time and another guy who followed her all the way to San Diego just to be with her... Imagine? How blessed can this girl be? She never runs out of man!!! 
 Anyway, the book was average. Nothing too blissful! Nothing get addicted about! It was a good story but I just wished the author didn't squeezed in everything. It was too long, as if she's writing for a screenplay already. Sometimes it's good to be thrilled about something. Sometimes it's nice to keep the anticipation. It gets to lanky to feed everything to your readers.

3 B's for this book. Breathless,Beautiful and Brilliant. Colleen Hoover, I won't tire from saying that you are indeed a literature genius. Everything's brilliant in what you've written. From Slammed to Point of Retreat and now with Hopeless, I'm in awe of you! Truly!!! 
 The book made me feel different emotions in a superlative level. The amount of happiness that this book brought me was incomparable, the sadness that was painted in my face during the most heart breaking scenes was immeasurable. 
 Although, I admit it was too heavy for me. The burden that Sky was holding was indeed too heavy but I admire the character for having been able to surpass it. It's an inspiration for us that no matter how tough we're going through in life we just got to be strong and never let our fear of the unkown consume us because by the end of the day it's us who'll feel fulfillment and freedom once we've surpassed our problems. 
 I really love how Colleen Hoover made me see man differently. Holder, I love you!!! He never gave up on Sky despite all the shit she's been holding up. He was there for her every step of the way. He's words were so wise that made me say, "I hope I'll find someone like Holder" because he says the right words not to flatter you but make you realize. 
 The words were perfectly written, very wise indeed. It made me realize a lot of things. And I believe it's a measure that the book was able to deliver the message it wants to convey to its readers, once the reader understood and applied it to his/her own life. 
 There were flaws...but the amount of flaws in not tantamount to how brilliant the book is. 
 5++++ stars for this!!!

Is there any rating higher than 5 because I will butterflying give that rating to this book! I read the book around 11pm and I couldn't stop reading it. My eyes were already tired but I forced myself to finish reading this book because it's so damn good!!! 
 Let me commend Colleen Hoover. Colleen Hoover, you ought to write a sequel for this or perhaps write more stories because you are one butterfly of a writer. You are a literature genius! I love your treatment on this sequel. This time Will speaks and I love how you transformed a male character in this story because normally boys in every story are known to be less clingy, they're known to be tough, they're not a fan of romance and PDA, they're completely guarded. But with this book, you made me think of boys differently and I hope there's someone out there who is like Will. 
 I love how things worked differently between Will and Lake, they're madly in love with each other that they couldn't get their hands off each other. 
 I love that there's a new member to the gang. Kristien. I hope I had her name right. She's butterflying smart and it's like a body of an older person possesses her whenever she speaks. She speaks of truth and her knowledge is way beyond her age. And I love that Kel is her boyfriend. 
 I love that there were a lot of spice added to their relationship. The preview, the countdown, the way Will stares to Lake, the way Lake would just attack Will with a kiss, the surprises, the stars which's timing is so right to their problems, the bitch Vaughn, the bitch best friend of Will, the slam, oh the list is endless. 
 I love how Will did a lot of dumb things to patch things between him and Lake. As in a of dumb things, hiring an eleven year old to patch things up between you and your girlfriend? Seriously? 
 I love the strength that Will have shown during the roughest time of his life. How he never left Lake, how much he has shown that Lake is everything to him, how he handled such a big problem that isn't in anyone's hand anymore.... I believe he got through to all of those because of his love to Lake. Oww!! 
 I love Lake's stubbornness! 
 I love Grandpaul!! His humor!! He had one of this "intelligent phones" Hahaha!! And he asked Will to just tweet his problems to him. And he has a tweeter account and he's being followed by the President. 
 I love every time they say I love you to each other.... Say it again... Omy! I tears my heart!!! 
 This is one of the best books I've ever read!!!

There's so much to love about this book. But it would be unfair to point out what is so-called "the best" because every part of the story will make you think, will make you realize, will make you wonder, will make you love, will make you care and will make you appreciate life. It was beautifully written and a story well thought of. 
 It's not just a love story. But it's a love story with a lot of ingredients added to it that makes the story great. It talks about pain, loss, acceptance, friendship, poetry and life.

This book left me nothing but a heavy and confused heart!!! Gah! This is love to the next level! Now I realized that one can be selfish when it comes to love. One can be greedy when it comes to love. And one is willing to risk it all when it comes to love! 
 Olivia is one hell of a confused girl. She shoves Caleb away from her then one day she's doing everything to win him back and then mess things up and break up with him then win him back again then mess things up again... It's a pathetic and strenuous cycle! I guess the reason why she's too guarded it's because of what happened to her family. He's father has always cheated on her mother that she even witnessed the cheating unfold in front of her. The kind of love she has grown with is not the kind of love that anyone of us is experiencing. She's confused as to what love is. 
 Caleb, you're one hell of a romantic guy! But I hate you because you're one hell of a womanizer! How dare you? I fell in love with you! But how could you? You could've fought even harder for the girl you want... You just let things slip in the way. 
 I really can't fathom my feelings with this book. I love how I get accustomed to different emotions when I read this book. I just felt like reading this book was like taking a roller coaster ride, there were a lot of highs and lows in this book. Its a good thing because it leaves you curious and it leaves you wanting more. 
 I wish this has a sequel! Gah!!! 
 Wanna take a roller coaster ride? Read this book!

I was in a bookstore searching, inquiring, going through all the stalls for Colleen Hoover's books but the battle search just lead me into this book. I knew right away when I saw this book that I've marked it as my "to read" book. With the money intended to buy Colleen Hoover's books but since there aren't available yet, I gambled on this book. It's quite expensive from its neighboring paperbacks but I know there was something special about this book that made me want to buy it. I actually held it for awhile because I might come across with lesser valued book with a great story but I just saw myself standing in front of the cashier, grabbing a grand, the bar code scanned, handing the money to the girl, have the amount typed, handing me my change, get's the receipt, putting the book inside the brown paper bag with red print and grabbing the item and shoving it inside my bag. So in short, I bought it... 
 Anyway, ever since I read Anna and the French Kiss I got so in love with Paris! That I started buying a planner with the Eiffel Tower emblazoned on it, sticky notes with anything Paris, pens and a lot more!!! I got so excited when I knew that one of the settings of the book is in Paris... but not like other books which's story often happens in the Eiffel Tower, Lourve, Notre Dame... the book touched on places I've never heard but got my interest into it. It showed a different facet of Paris. A facet that only a true Parisian can tell but was successfully put into words and descriptively liven up by the writer. 
 The book was more on self-discovery and having a say in Life. Allyson, unfortunately, had her life plotted chronologically by her parents. She was the kind of daughter who every parents want to have. Obedient, understanding, respectful, studious, submissive, adventure averse person, good girl... Until after she arrived from her European tour that everything that she was once known started making her ask herself if that's the kind of girl she still wants to be or if she wants to be the person she has made herself up when she was in Paris.... Care free, independent, happy, always thirsty for adventure! 
 I'd like to elaborate more on this book but I'd be giving out spoilers. Anyway, I love how this book was different from those that I have read. I love how she has found herself during her journey and how far she came to find the answers to her year long questions and she has transformed herself to becoming the person she always want to be.

The story was too heavy for me. I pushed myself to finish reading this book because it'll leave me with a heavy heart. The things that happened to Echo's life was way too HEAVY and I couldn't imagine what my life would be if I had hers. Same goes to Noah. Their lives were full of misery but when they found each other, they turned their miseries into happiness. It's just nice to know that in this chaotic world, you'll always find someone who shares the same misery as yours, same happiness as yours and shares the same passion and love as yours. I like that every chapter Echo and Noah got to speak. I just got annoyed with the friends of Noah. But hey! It was a good book but too heavy though.

My hopes were high with this book. Judging from the plot, the reviews, the ratings. I thought I already found a book better than Slammed and Point of Retreat. But I was disappointed :( 
 The shift of the story was too abrupt and I can't identify whether it's still part of the previous scene or is it a new one... There were a lot of problems that weren't resolved in the story like what happened between Nan and Sam? Are they gonna still be friends? Have the Garret's forgiven Sam's mother? What happened to Tim? Was he able to successfully get out of his parents lives and have a fresh start? The story just simply ended without resolutions to the problem. 
 The story has already built its momentum when the accident happened. But eventually, the momentum disappeared and all was left was doubts and questions in your mind... Arghh!! 
 The scumbag man, I forgot his name! The campaign adviser of Sam's mom! He's a dick! I hate him, he's very unforgiving and inhumane! How can such person exist? 
 Somehow, there were also interesting parts in the story. Like when Jase and Sam finally met after how many years of thinking the other doesn't exist. When they finally kissed! When they did it... The awkward part when they both bought the tampon and couldn't decide which to choose because they were both innocent in such thing. When Jase kept on thinking what happened the other night, when they did it, he was completely distracted he hammered his thumb and Sam kissed it and Jase kept on saying he had an injury in some other parts which Sam all kissed. Gah! 
 I also love Will, the walking encyclopedia of the family, he never runs out of trivia! He's such a great child!! I never knew that when you drop a coin from the Empire State Building someone will die! Such a wiz! 
 Anyway, the book wasn't like what I expected it to be... However, it was good.

The start of the book was quite slow and I didn't grasped what it was trying to imply to its readers. I didn't liked her fashion sense, referring to Lola and her dirty punk rock boyfriend, Max. The book only got interesting on the part where Cricket started appearing. 
 This book established Perkins identity to her readers. She's fond of writing stories on unrequited love. 
 I like how she inserted Anna and Etienne on the story. I like how their relationship progresses. Etienne is now thinking of their future which is kinda cute because knowing that they are still young but they already foresee the future of being together. 
 Over-all, it was average. Not the same impact it created on me on the first book.

I love-hate this book! I love this book because it shows that, a lot of things can happen and these things happen in the least you expect it. It's a different treatment on teenage love stories. Before I mention everything I love, I'd like to talk about what are the things I hate about the book. It would've been nicer if it was a first person treatment. The main caharcter could've told the story so that the emotions were more humane, more personal and more intimate. 
 There were parts when she told the story about herself, the narration was too much that it gets boring. If the author treated it in a personal context, people would've cared for her and understood where her emotions come from. 
 I love the kissing part! I love how Oliver was just so real and he really just can't contain his feelings that he just bursted into kissing Hadley. I love how they can just talk about topics people normally talk about when they reached years of being together. They're only random people but they talk as if its forever. 
 Over-all, this book is an interesting book to read.

For giggle and romantic part, I'd like to rate it 3 because it's so lame to know that Roger and Amy have to fell in love towards the end of the story. But, however, I love how Amy has to pour in all of the pain that was welling up on her to Roger so that she can gauge if Roger is really someone for keeps. When Roger accepted and in fact pointed out to Amy that she wasn't cause of her father's death, that was when Amy let her walls come down and just felt the urge of becoming reckless and kissed Roger as if her life depends on it. 
 For the treatment of scenes, I like how Morgan Matson put flashbacks every end of a chapter so that the readers will know how the events from the previous chapter occured and how was it triggered. 
 For the use of words, I'd say it was good but somehow I felt like Morgan was afraid to use difficult words because her book's target audience are the teenagers. It's important for you to know the language that your target audiences speak so that you'll know how to make use of your vocabulary and you'll know what to write and what you ought not to write. 
 For the uniqueness, I'd rate it 4.5 because of naming the chapter as CHAPTER 1, etc. The author put quotes that'll explain what the chapter is all about. Well, not necessarily explain but somehow would put to sense what the whole chapter tries to imply. 
 For the lessons I've learned, I'd rate it 5. There's just to much to learn from the book. It felt like it was a multi-faceted book. 
 "The best discoveries always happened to the people who weren't looking for it." 
 "It's not about the destination. It's getting there that's the good part. 
 "We can't know what's going to happen. We can just try to figure it out as we go along.

I love how simple the story was told but the meaning of each words leave you think and make you realize. Auggie was indeed the epitome of courage, strength and wisdom. I love how each of the key characters had a chapter to show their own perspective. And each of them lead to one thing, their love and concern for Auggie. I really broke down on the graduation part. It was really a heart breaking scene and I can picture out how people who use to insult him, who use to talk behind his back and who use to scare away from him as if he has a contagious disease.

I love Gossip Girl series. I've been hooked since high school. My sense of fashion has been greatly influenced by Serena and confidence by Blair. Although there were quite changes when it was on series. I already expected it to be as such but nevertheless, I still liked it. Although it was too short, it seems like I was just given a glimpse of all the worst that might happen on the following books.

We should see with our hearts not with our eyes. This is the lesson I've learned from reading The Little Prince. I was convinced to read this book because my favorite professor, Sir Elson, told me that this was his favorite book. I've been hearing about this book and I was expecting it to be thick and in hard bound. But to my surprise, it was just thin. You can finish reading it in a couple of hours. I love that there were illustrations! It teaches a lot of lessons. Such an awe-inspiring book.

... If I woke up in a different body every day-if you never knew what I was going to like tomorrow-would you still love me? 
 That line in the book tore my heart apart. Simple for us to utter words but it's hard to do it. And it even gets harder when you're actually in the situation wherein you have to choose from being with the only person you've loved so much but you have to carry the burden of seeing him in different bodies everyday or get away from that person but you're heart is shattered into pieces every time you're not with him. 
 There's so many things to love about this book. ...I love the anticipation it gives me, I'm excited to know what body A inhabits this time. I love how A save the lives of the helpless people he inhabits and how he completely make things memorable before he leaves the body he inhabits. I love how he makes an effort to see Rhiannon every time he gets a chance, I love the effort that Rhi has to put through just to see A. I love the strength and courage that Rhi showed, it's definitely hard... Really it is. You have kept a lot of things from people because you know they wont believe you otherwise, the pain of not being able to introduce A to her friends because she knows the next day he'll be a different person, the pain of not being able to stay the night with him and wake up the next morning with him because there are so many risks, the pain of not being able to introduce him to your parents and the pain of loving someone but he's different, physically, every day. 
 One of the most painful parts of the book was when A attended the funeral of the grand father he inhabited. Clearly, he's not directly related to this person but all of the sudden he just cries during the eulogy not because he felt for the death of the grand father but because he realized, he'll never experience the things that the old man is experiencing. When A dies, no one will speak good things about him, no one will tell them about the craziest and most memorable experiences they had, no one will feel like there's someone missing in their lives and no one will cry for him when he dies. 
 I love the part when he inhabited the body of Alexander. My favorite body conquest. He told Rhi that they'll meet in the bookstore and pretend like it's the first time they met so that these are the memories he's going to leave to Alexander. He chose Alexander to take care of Rhi because he knows that Rhi and Alex shares the same passion and he knows that Alexander will give the same amount of love that A has given to Rhi. They started counting the remaining minutes until midnight, Rhi kept kissing A. Gosh! If only I can put my emotions here and share to you how much pain I felt and tears that fell when I read this part. Indescribable.

I.LOVE.THIS.BOOK. I was only starting to read the book but I immediately got hooked. It's like I don't want to stop from reading it because I felt hanging. I was in a train ride when I was reading this, I grinned like an idiot and if I was the only person in the train, I would've started screaming and giggling. There's too many great scenes. There were also scenes I got too emotional. I don't want to stop reading this book but there's also a part of me who wants to stagger reading this book. The most painful part for me, as a reader, is that when you have established a bubble for you and the book it felt like there's only two things... You and the book... and when you are almost finished, you have a fear that "that" bubble you have established will just pop out. 
 I love how Stephanie Perkins connected with her readers. Her choice of words were impeccable, the lines were simple yet striking, her jokes were funny and everything was real and you can feel the emotions of the characters. 
 I also love that she introduced Parisian culture, breath-taking landmarks and a lot if information I only knew when I read the book. It makes you want to go to Paris as soon as possible! 
 I love how she also mentioned a lot of movies. Haven't heard any of those from the book but I think I'll check them out. 
 Anna and Etienne are among my favorite book couples. Their relationship has definitely evolved. Update: April 12, 2014 
 OKAY, so I think it was yesterday (April 11, 2014)that Lionsgate announced that Allegiant is going to be TWO MOVIES . And I'm in awe. Looking back at what I thought about this book not too long ago, I'm wondering why I felt that way. WHY, PAST SELF??! WHY???!?!11 
 A lot has changed since then, primarily after Divergent became a movie. After Divergent became popular. After Divergent became the next Hunger Games . (TRUST ME, I DON'T WANT TO COMPARE IT TO THG, BUT HEY, THATS THE MEDIA'S WAY OF TALKING, SO WHY NOT USE IT?) 
 I never thought I'd feel this way, but this is how I feel now. And I don't think that will change. 
 Okay. Last March 20 I watched Divergent because it's one of my favorite novels. It will always be one of my favorite novels and that will never change. I wasn't in the fangirl mood concerning the movie, though. I never was, actually. I was just really happy that my favorite book was beoming a movie. Shailene? I prefer her as Hazel from The Fault in Our Stars . Theo? I don't think he'll ever be Four , but beggars can't be choosers. 
 The movie is like 2 hours long and they covered pretty much most of the scenes in Divergent but after it ended I was left there thinking... dumbfounded... 
 Divergent wasn't the best adaptation. It's my opinion. I wasn't wowed! by it. I didn't cry. I sure didn't laugh. I didn't feel any intense emotion while watching the movie. Movies are suppose to make you feel something, right? This movie did made me feel something: Disappointment. A letdown. I overestimated the movie. i overestimated Lionsgate. I overestimated you, from the studio of THG! 
 So now you must be thinking: You're not reviewing the book but the movie! I'm getting there, okay? So after the movie and after this huge announcement above I double thought the whole entire trilogy. This trilogy that made me laugh, cry, fangirl, squeal, facepalm, etc etc. I asked myself questions: 
 "Why the hype?" 
 "Was it even that good, like super good?" 
 "Think about it: seriously, what was the whole deal about the GP and GD??" 
 "Do you really really like it? Or did you liked it because everyone else did?" 
 I'm not going to lie: The Divergent Movie made me rethink about what I thought about the book itself and I wished it didn't let me but it did. And from five stars, I'm going down to two stars. And I'll explain why: 
 FROM WHAT I REMEMBER FROM ALLEGIANT, they go to this place outside of Chicago, something like the Omega Point from Unravel Me . (That's the best analogy I could think of, considering I recently read the Shatter Me trilogy a couple of months ago.) From this point I don't really remember much: more making out sessions with Tobias, more lame talking, etc etc, more history to be dealt with, blah.... 
 OH BUT I DO REMEMBER SOMETHING. WHEN URIAH GETS KILLED OFF. BECAUSE OF A SPECIAL SOMEONE WHO LISTENED TO A SOMEONE WHO'S NOT EVEN THAT RELEVANT EVEN THOUGH A CERTAIN PERSON TOLD THE SOMEONE NOT TO LISTEN TO THAT SOMEONE. 
 Yes, I remember now. Tobias was my biggest problem with the book, hands down. This is no lie. Even as I began reading Allegiant for the first time, I started to dislike Tobias. (So much for dual POV) His personality was totally messed up, man! UUGHHHHH ANGER IS FLOWING and IDC that his pretty Tris died I seriously did not like his attitude in this book.  Before I start let me just point out some of my favorite quotes in Veronica Roth's finale, Allegiant: 
 1. "and I know the beauty he sees is just freedom -- freedom to be seen as a whole man instead of a damaged one." Tobias, 248 
 2. "It's strange, but there's something in that thought that makes me feel almost ...free." Tris, 187

 IF YOU DIDN'T READ DIVERGENT AND INSURGENT, THEN YOU REALLY SHOULD! 
 At this point, don't read this if you didn't read Allegiant! 
 In Allegiant, you will discover: 
 1. Lies, betrayal, and deceit. 
 2. The meaning behind Allegiant, as usual in all of the books. 
 3. How being Divergent just separates you from everyone else. 
 4. How being different from one another can lead to conflict. 
 5. The truth behind being a Dauntless... if you know what I mean. 
 6. Sacrifice to save one another. 
 7. and an unexpected ending. For me, I knew that either Tris or Tobias would pass, but I didn't expect it to be that drastic. 
 I feel like everything inside of me has been shattered because I haven't been attached to a book for so long. (The Fault in Our Stars is the first one.) There's just so much emotion in Allegiant that you're going to laugh, cry, fangirl, get mad, say no, say yes... 
 To further explain my feelings towards this book, I will do this through describing some characters in Allegiant. 
 Tris: She is the bravest character in Allegiant, hands down. I admire how deep her love and affection is towards her family and friends. I learned that to sacrifice is to show the greatest love for all. Yes, I was weeping when Veronica killed her off, but then if she lived, it wouldn't really feel realistic. Life is never easy. 
 Tobias: I started to hate him when he listened to Nita, instead of Tris. Because of the explosions my favorite character, Uriah, died. But then I admire him. He shows he's all strong and mighty, while in fact he is suffering in the inside. Reading his POV at the ending was very painful to bear. 
 Christina: Being Christina seriously sucks. Will and Uriah died and they were Christina's close friends. But then, just as what she said at the last page of the book, She's holding on to the moments that do not suck. The trick is to notice them when they come around. 
 Peter: Peter is one of my favorite characters ever since Divergent. I liked him because of his cruel and sinister personality, and after he swallowed the memory serum, I admired him even more because he realized that his doings were wrong, but then he can't do anything to change himself either. There are just some habits that will never go away, and when you're given the chance to take away with it by erasing memory, you have a choice to do so or not. I would take that choice, absolutely. 
 David: I think there was a point in his life where he could have just turned back time and maybe had a family with Natalie or something. Nothing hurts more than watching the one you love with another. But then love is also about making sure that person is at her happiest. Regarding about the experiments, it feels like that's the only thing keeping him going, now that Natalie is gone. And also that he is the head, he has the power. 
 Uriah: Okay, I should point out right now that Uriah and Peter are my favorite characters in the whole Divergent series. So when Zeke told Tobias to look after him, Veronica just gave me a dead giveaway that Uriah was going to die soon. Just when he was getting cozy with Christina... We didn't get to hear his famous last words! 
 Nita: I'm trying to figure out what to say about Nita... did her action proved her heroic or not? I don't know, maybe she was only thinking about the only option, but not the option that could save everyone, unlike Tris. I would love to learn more about her, actually. 
 All in all, the Divergent series was a success! I liked how in the end, there was no war because they were able to stop it before it happened. I liked how they tried to think of ways that would save more people instead of just one (as what Tris says.) It was only 2 chapters until the epilogue and I already missed reading from the mind of Tris. I'm pretty sure everyone misses her.

HHhH charms with its brilliance and capivates with its whim. The atrocities committed by Heydrich and those under his command are well known but surprisingly little is known about the brave men and women whose mission it was to end his reign of terror. 
 What is especially impressive about HHhH is how Binet tries to tell this remarkable story. All too often historical fiction and even historical work is tarnished by convenient untruths and grandiose embellishment. 
 Against this, HHhH is refreshing with its attempt to encourage the reader to reconstruct the truth surrounding the assassination attempt on Heydrich, even though our protagonist effectively deconstructs everything that he encounters in order to allow the reader to do so. Yet there are times where our protagonist cannot help himself and indulges in the dramatic flourish that he rails against. It is at these moments where the reader can appreciate the difficulty that storytellers face in capturing a true account of events 
 Personally I would be more inclined to dabble into historical fiction if its storytelling style continues along this new exciting path set down by Binet.

Well, where do I even start.

Turns out, this book is filled with a made up language based off of Russian slang. I saw some reviews praising the author for making the slang accessible and easy to follow and learn. All I have to say about that is 'speak for yourself.' I had no idea how to read this and I was barely getting along until I finally looked up a glossary and memorized a few of the more commonly used words. 
 Besides the difficulty I faced in reading this book, I guess I just don't "get it." The ultraviolence turned me off, which I guess was the point, however, I know a lot of people felt sorry for Alex and what he went through, well, not me. I'm not saying he deserved everything he got, but he deserved a lot of it. He was a borderline psychopath who got off on violence and being an overall shitty human being. I have no sympathy for what he went through. I think what made me lose any and all compassion I might have had for him is when he got two 10 year old girls drunk, brought them home, then raped them. 
 I don't get the theme warning about government control and whatever -- maybe they crossed the line but it's hard to care when the only example of that we're showed is what happened to Alex. 
 Overall, I thought this book sucked. I almost gave up after page 20 but I powered through thinking about all the good reviews on goodreads. In hindsight, I should have just read wikipedia. This book was a real pain in the ass to read. If anyone wants to try and explain to me whatever I'm not seeing, that'd be nice. Can't say I'd agree with you, though.

 3.5 stars. Okay. This book was a pretty solid 4 stars until the ending. I mean, if you read this book for what it is, you'll really enjoy it. What it is is a nice, easy, mindless, chick-lit book. It's a fast, easy read full of fluff and light teenage angst. So, I accepted that fact and I really enjoyed the book. The writing made me chuckle sometimes out loud but there were also times where I thought it was pretty cheesy (even for a chick-lit) and wondered if a guy really acted that way or would say that. Usually books with characters like these just annoy the crap out of me but somehow when Lauren Barnholdt writes them it's okay. Now, let's move on to the ending/my rant. Seriously, this book went from a solid 4 stars to 3/3.5 stars. I mean, I'd give the ending itself 2 stars. Obviously I said not to expect much from this book but I seriously expected more than what it is. Let me explain. Jace and Peyton hook up for one day but it's this crazy, out of this world, amazing day. Then they talk and whatnot. Then one day, Jace stops talking to her, and therefore, breaks up with her (even though they technically weren't even dating). And it's like Jace and Peyton still aren't over each other *cue eye roll* and somehow they end up on this sorta, kinda road trip together. Oh, and you find out they broke up because of this "secret" that Peyton kept from Jace...prepare for the ranting (It will most definitely contain spoilers so...) It turns out the "secret" that Peyton kept from Jace was that her parents were getting a divorce. What. The. Actual. Fuck. Okay, here's where I have a problem with this book. I was willing to overlook the fact that Peyton and Jace are unrealistically obsessed with each other after one day but I will not overlook this. Like, SERIOUSLY? THAT'S WHY HE WAS PISSED OFF AT HER? Are you fucking kidding me? Well, first off Jace, considering you guys only went on one date, it's no fucking wonder she didn't tell you that her parents were getting a divorce . She barely fucking knows you. She didn't even tell ANYONE yet, not even her best friend, or close family members, and you fucking expect her to tell you something that personal?! It obviously must devastate her. Why the fuck would you feel like she was obligated to tell you? It wasn't even a secret in a sense. It was her not ready to fucking share everything with you. That's so fucking stupid. If that was me I'd tell the guy to fuck off. Not like I owe it to him to tell him something that's personal and none of his business, especially if I've only known him for a few months. 
 Also, Peyton was just so stupid. Why the fuck she didn't tell her dad, or anyone, that her mom stole her identity is beyond me. Yeah, I get it. that sucks. It was out of nowhere and how the hell do you confront a parent? But seriously, your dad is a fucking option! HELLO?! I mean, yeah, take some time to digest it but completely doing nothing about it and "running away" is just ridiculous. How old is she again? 
 And Jordan giving that advice to Jace? Do teenage guys even think like that? And Jace and Peyton's povs sounded really similar. 
 There are plenty more things to complain about but I think it'll just take all day. I gave Two-Way Street (a similar book by the same author) 5 stars because I read it years ago when I was much younger and my tastes were not yet as mature and refined as they are now (pfft hahahahahaha. yeah right. like I can actually use the words mature and refined to describe myself. Probably more accurate to say I've slightly matured from pre-teen to young adult teen and therefore, now enjoy deeper reads.I still enjoy chick-lit every now and then though.), and the book was easy to read (I started and finished it on a Saturday morning) but I'm pretty sure if I re-read it now the rating would go down. Still, if you read the book for what it is and aren't expecting anything above superficiality then you'll be able to enjoy the book. 
 Plus there were a lot of things that didn't have closure. Also, why the heck even have B.J. in the book? And that scene with Jace's mom. Talk about cheesy and unrealistic. 
 Also the cameos with Courtney and Jordan seemed to be there just so they would have a cameo in the book. Lame.

*Sigh* Boy, was I disappointed from this book...I was expecting this book to be amazing because it has a pretty high rating (honestly, I should have learned my lesson from TFiOS) and that some reviewers that I follow have praised and lauded Ms. Stiefvater's other books. So, I obviously expected this book to be amazing. I was wrong. It was boring, lackluster, and plain. First off, the pacing. Literally nothing, NOTHING, happens in this book. Oh you can argue with that point but whatever. I first realized that nothing happened at around page 100 when Puck had FINALLY decided to register in the race on her regular horse. It's ridiculous that it took that long. Why? Because it's unnecessary and BECAUSE IT'S EXPLAINED IN THE SYNOPSIS. Ugh. Such a bad move. Then I read 300 more pages and I got near the end when finally, FINALLY, the race actually started. 
 ...Are you kidding me? The WHOLE book is superficial and composed of NOTHING. Seriously!! I get it, the men discriminate against you, Puck, because you're a girl. I understood that concept the first time it happened. No need to shove it in my face every chapter. You and Sean have this crazy love for horses that no one else apparently understands. Gotcha. Oh yeah, and it's a BIG deal because you're the first/only girl to decide to do this. Yeah, I GOT THE MEMO. The idea that a girl takes the first initiative to end something that has long time been a male dominated activity used to be original but now it's become cliche, expected even! The author literally could have written this book in like 100 pages or less. Seriously. (Also, the reason that Puck joined the races is incredibly stupid and shallow. Seriously? It's not believable enough for me.) 
 The author writes this book in alternating point of views. Puck and Sean. A.k.a. the female protagonist who is defying gender roles blah blah blah (not that that's not important but the way it was written was quite honestly, lame) and the male love interest (oh please, that's not even a spoiler. Seriously, did anyone NOT expect them to get together?) because you've got to add a little romance in here *sarcasm*. My main complaint with this style choice is that the tone of the povs ARE EXACTLY THE SAME. Sean and Puck sound exactly.the.same. I shit you not, I'm not even exaggerating or anything. I swear. Honest. I mean, if you're going to write multiple povs you HAVE to write them so they're different from one another (I think Rick Riordan is a GREAT example of this. His characters in the HoO series [while not all likable, at least to me] definitely all have unique voices. It's practically impossible to get them mixed up). Seriously, it's only two characters! You seriously couldn't create two different personalities? I mean, there's this one page where Sean remarks on how handsome this American guy is (another thing, the author created this world and decided to incorporate it somehow with reality. It's weird and awkward, at least for me). Do guys even do that?! 
 I did enjoy the ending but it definitely DOES NOT make up for reading a whole book worth of nothing. The ending, while pleasing, isn't even surprising either. It's expected. Not good. 
 This book unfortunately lacks originality. It falls into that young-adult-book category (I can't think of the word right now). Y'know, when all young adult books seem to follow this pattern? Boy-meets-girl or vice versa and they bond and they get together at the end and everything works out happily ever after after stumbling over a few conflicts here or there. I can't articulate myself right now but...yeah.
Odysseus is such an arrogant, power-hungry manwhore.

It was a very clever addition that worked out because the other povs give us insight in how other people perceive August's facial deformities. It works so well because the author was spot on in her characterization of the characters. Their thoughts and their actions were 100% accurate/realistic and completely reflect how kids (and even adults) would act or think. Honestly, reading this transported me back to when I was in elementary school and I honestly emphasize so much. I was definitely one of those kids who didn't partake in bullying but I wouldn't stand up for the person either (I'm ashamed to say). 
 Kids and adults alike will enjoy this book and the message resonates no matter how old one may be. Everyone should be reminded of the message of this book and I genuinely think if I ever have a child/children I'm going to give them this book to read. I honestly teared up like twice throughout this book, but I'm a big sap, so.

But the Celeana we read isn't that, sure she has her moments but for the most part it's HUGE telling-not-showing. For the full experience I HIGHLY suggest reading the novellas first! You won't regret it :D (seriously I enjoyed the novellas more than this book). still, looking forward to the next one. Also let it be known that I read this book around right when it came out and I PREDICT CHAOL WILL END UP WITH CELAENA IN THE END. That's right, I can already tell Chaol will end up with her, and I will feel shamelessly vindicated when this happens in the end. But I'm Team Dorian anyways :p

4.5 stars...or 5? This book was REALLY uncomfortable for me to read (mostly the beginning) . Especially since this book portrays the abuser as someone who is so different than how it is normally portrayed. For example, in most books, if the main character (usually a girl, haven't read one about a boy yet but who knows)is sexually abused, it is usually by maybe a close male figure. Nope, not in this book (kinda). So, kudos to the author. Leah was a mystery for me. I felt like I knew her personality and why she does what she does but then she does something or says something and I'm back to square one. I'm just as lost as Laine as to Leah's personality. I knew or I FELT really that she was being abused by Sam because of the seemingly obvious hints but then later I would be so unsure of myself. Like what I thought the reason for something happening wasn't actually the reason at all. Really, I felt like Laine, I felt like Leah was manipulating me (so, that's amazing. I mean, for a book to make me feel like the protagonist does? For me to have my feelings and thoughts manipulated? It doesn't sound like a good thing but I don't think a book has ever made me feel that way as strongly as this book does). In the beginning I was annoyed at Laine for being so weak. I thought Leah was just a manipulative b**ch oh sure, she's a victim yes but in the end she was still a manipulative b**ch. Yes, she was probably that way because of the things she experience but still...Somehow by the middle of the book I was SYMPATHIZING with her. I felt sorry for her, even though I still looked down at her for how she treated Laine. It's complicated.

Unsure whether or not to rate this 4 or 5 stars. For sure though, this book is not for everyone. Especially if you disagree with the main character's views (political, religious etc). Personally there were times I couldn't stand Cole and was in disbelief as to why Ashley just accepted what happened. If there's one thing to learn from this book is that love demands sacrifice and compromise.

2nd readthrough: 3.5 stars. 
 Every time I reread an Ellen Hopkins novel I notice something new about the formatting that I didn't notice before (or maybe I did notice but just didn't mention it?). For example, during my second read through of this book, about 3/4 of the way through, I realized (or re-realized?) that each of the 5 narrators have different formatting for their POV! How cool is that! It always amazes me how Ellen Hopkins can write books like these; it must take an insane amount of attention to detail.
I like to call this book the "mind fuck" book...

DNF - read up to page 203. 
 I tried. I just can't do it. This book is just so BORING. I don't care about any of the characters, especially Amy (who is narrating the book). The story is supposedly some journey to self healing and re-self discovery but I read 2/3 of the book and the journey has barely even begun. I don't understand what all the hype is about and I wish I gave up earlier instead of wasting my time trying to power through this. I should have known this book sucked since the beginning.

Holy shit. Oh, my gosh. That ending. It was so EPIC. The story was epic and the characters were fleshed out and well-written. There was never a boring part and I think I really need to start watching the show (at least season 1) so I can actually see the epic battles and sword fights taking place. The hype for this book is well placed. So many plot twists. A lot of political intrigue that I wasn't expecting but very much enjoyed. Looking forward to the next books.
I remember reading this in 5th grade...I shall re-read it one day

I didn't like this book. I didn't like the plot, the characters, the main character, or the love interest. Actually, Bianca's best friends were probably the most likable people in this book. Bianca is such a judgmental bitch. And she has this insane inferiority complex throughout the whole book. The characters are all really one dimensional and it was really hard to feel sympathy for her having to deal with her parent's divorce . The synopsis sounded interesting, but the book itself, however, is not. I'm disappointed. I was expecting so much more and I kept reading because of some naive, misguided hope that it would get better (It didn't). *sigh* I only pushed through it because in the movie they're making they casted Robbie Amell *swoon* as Wesely. And he's like my biggest celebrity crush, ever since he was on Life With Derek. Ahh enough about my life story. I simply didn't care for, nor like this book in the slightest, and Bianca is so unlikable, how can you root for her? (I couldn't). Also, the characters seemed so unrealistic. Seriously.

I'm conflicted on how many stars to rate this book. Overall 3.5. It was a nice read and it's pretty strong considering this is Ms. Fitzpatrick's debut novel. BUT, it's nothing I haven't read before. Oh sure there was that one twist when what's her face's mom hits Jase's father. I just finished the book and I forgot the main character's name... looked it up and it's Sam. but it's still the same story, boy meets girl (or more accurately girl meets boy), boy and girl fall in love, either boy or girl does something or something happens then they break up and one of them is heartbroken, in the end boy and girl reconcile and fall happily in love. The end. Don't mean to sell this book short but it's nothing new to me. 
 is still my quintessential summer romance book this year. This book is still worth reading though, I mean, IT HAS A LARA CROFT REFERENCE!

I came up with a new shelf because of this book "Annoying protagonists". This book was really quick and easy to read. My main problem is Ann is so naive and dense that I was literally raising my voice at the book... Seriously, she could have saved all that trouble by killing mr. loomis. She just let him come in HER home (literally) and SHE was the one who left. She let him come and take over everything she had and she let him run her out. . There was one part where I laughed, not necessarily because it was meant to be funny (maybe it was but I doubt it) but because it was just so stupid. where Faro was tracking her to the cave and she realized that she had to kill, no not Mr. Loomis, the guy who was making her life a living hell, but the dog who didn't even realize anything was wrong. *EXTREME MELODRAMATIC SIGH* *shaking of the head* . Heard they're making a movie with Amanda Seyfried and Chris Pine, can't wait to watch it!
3.5 stars. The ending kind of reminded me of Lord of the Flies...
It's 3 in the morning and I'm happy/sad crying. I love this book.
Aww fluffyness level= max. Oh, and the protagonist has some raging hormones...

I loved loved loved loved loved loved LOVED this book. Katsa was such a BAMF and Po was extremely likable and Bitterblue was already a BAMF-in-training. Also, the antagonist was really well done. I sincerely despise him and reading the prologue of Fire intensifies this. Well done Ms. Cashore! 
 It is about time I read this. It's been on my to-read list far too long (think 3+ years!) No more putting it off. It's time.

Team Jem...or I will burn the book and throw it against the wall. 
 *During reading* 
 Found 2 typos, on page 275 and on page 279. Mrs. Clare seems to have mixed up Gabriel and Gideon :p
