While the first part of the book intrigues, the latter portion disappoints. As a avid follower of history, naturally I seek answers to the several questions he poses in the book. But I don't agree with cherry-picking history to come up with causations that suit a narrative and for that reason, the book falls short in my eyes

Details the evolution of IBM , the original tech darling of Wall Street, through the eyes of it's inspirational founder Thomas Watson. Armed with a number of idiosyncrasies (not least a healthy dose of arrogance and narcissism), Watson made two huge gambles that in hindsight led to IBM's rise as the world's foremost engineering company. First, he invested heavily in capacity at the peak of the Depression gobbling up talent when no one else was hiring. Second, he massively added capacity during WWII, defying economists that predicted a post-war recession would lead to a drop in industrial demand. In both cases, the anti-consensus gamble worked out with IBM turning uncertainty into a market opportunity. A key lesson for any budding entrepreneurs - Always take calculated gambles and bet the house on it when you do.

This book is one of the most fascinating books I've read because it tries to resolve the dichotomy between prediction (a condition possible only in a deterministic world) and complexity ( which tells us that in a second order system, there is a certain futility to predicting the future because of the Butterfly Effect). 
 Using real-data sponsored by US Intelligence following the intelligence disaster that was the Iraq war , Mr Tetlock argues for a middle path and proves it using the scientific method of forecasting, analyzing, improving and repeating. Super forecasters exist because they follow the scientific method rigorously, are foxes rather than hedgehogs and have trained themselves to think of the future as a series of alternative worlds with a certain probability assigned to each case. 
 The real beauty of this book is that it encourages you to try to train yourself just like them but also warns that it is a function of who you are (people are foxes or hedgehogs by nature) and the limitations of the time scope of making prediction (It is impossible to predict the future 10 years hence because there are too many possible Lorenz attractors (or butterflies) that can cause fragility in your predictions)

Elon Musk is a visionary and a bully. He's an egoistical maniac that burns out his own staff and refuses to listen to anyone that questions his 'vision'. While great companies are usually built by demanding iconoclasts, Musk seems to be a combination of Houdini(for investors putting money into his companies) and a despot. Yes, Tesla is the sexiest car alive and SpaceX the most efficient way to get into space but the real question is can they scale before they lose everything? The jury is still out on Elon Musk.

I picked up this book because I was curious about the subject matter and the fact that it won the Man Booker prize for fiction.The book flows seamlessly as the author keeps weaving his tale of Munna , the Halwai, a poor village kid with a chequered past as he looks to strike it big in the new-age Indian economy.Old habits die hard in the country and in that respect , the author's potrayal of the different characters in the pantomine is accurate and well-researched.Written in the style of a Hemingway or a Pamuk , anyone growing up in the country can reflect upon the reality and the inherent contradictions that make up the different forms of Indian society. 
 That said , I believe the prose is in itself quite poor and while the writing makes for a light read , it has none of the literary depth of modern fiction greats like Hemingway or Marquez. Every issue that the author addresses such as hinduism , the north-south divide and corruption in the country is spoken of in an off-hand manner as he resorts to generic stereotypes to fit his narrative.Hemingway always said true emotions come from experience and the author's lack of experience in the difficult transition that India has had from a colonial society to an emerging market economy of a million entreprenuers, is evident. I wish Mr Adiga would have tried to dig deeper into the psychology of the rich man and the poor man rather than describing them at face value. 
 Like his social entreprenuer, I guess modern Indian fiction has to yet evolve into something capable of generating a modern literary masterpiece.On this evidence , I doubt that day is too far away.

A quick read. It took me a couple of hours to read through but my conclusions were that Peter Thiel and the PayPal Mafia really understand the ideas that make a business profitable and work to that blueprint , whether as investors or as entrepreneurs. And their track record is hard to debate so my advice to any want-to-be investors or entrepreneurs is one key question to think of is what is the hard question that this business is meant to solve?

Investing is an obsession and not a job.I think few exemplify that more than David Einhorn, one of the smartest fundamental investors in the current era. 
 In a world, where short-sellers are castigated as profiteers and trouble makers, Mr Einhorn demonstrates through his most public short that fundamental short-selling is the only tool to expose fraud and corruption in financial markets.His appeal to regulators to close loopholes that allow companies to feed off tax-payer dollars is genuine but it's difficult to be an optimist when incentives are so perverse despite all the outrage in the aftermath of the financial crisis.All I can say is that Mr Einhorn and his ilk, continue to be the de-facto regulators of a broken financial system and if they profit from that, well isn't it just right when you see the breadth of the work they put into doing so.

The power dynamics between the producer and the consumer is undergoing a paradigm shift as Chris Anderson explores in his 2008 book on the Long Tail of consumer demand.Never before has the consumer been in such control of his choices as major multinational corporations scramble to change from a standard push model to a pull model.Democratization of means of production and distribution has resulted in disruption to the traditional 80-20 model of revenue generation and the pioneers of the new digital world have been quick to realize that real revenue generation lies in the ability to aggregate and filter products in a world of abundance and not scarcity.Welcome to a world where the consumer just doesn't accept second-best anymore :D

I think Peter Lynch makes a lot of sense.It's something that very often we don't really try doing while investing in the stock market.Everyone wants to buy the news but if the news was going to make you a lot of money then wouldn't every speculator be rich? Stock picking is a long-term investment in a company that you believe adds sustainable value and is well-managed.If one believes otherwise , one might as well walk into the Bellagio in Vegas and try their luck there.

When asked about Newton's comment that he stood on the shoulders of giants,Einstein replied,"I don't agree with that.I stood on the shoulders of Maxwell."Perfectly summarising the outstanding contributions of Michael Faraday and James Clerk Maxwell in shaping the world today.Everything from lighting and power generation to space travel owes a debt to these two geniuses.The author spins a powerful tale of the importance of experimentation and a scientific temper as they set about revolutionising Newtonian science and usher in a new era of particle physics culminating in Einstein's formulation of the space time continuum.A delight to any science enthusiast and a source of inspiration to all those that aspire to work in theoretical Physics.

KKR's pursuit of RJR Nabisco has become part of Wall Street folklore, the culmination of a decade of extravagance and financial malfeasance.This classic book detailing the bidding process is a thriller, putting you in the shoes of the different players in the game and elaborates on the sheer madness that seemed to engulf Wall Street during the largest takeover in the era of megadeals.The biggest winners as Ross Johnson says,were the shareholders who enjoyed an early christmas present as the share price quadrupled during the bidding.For KKR , it was a pyrrhic victory as eventually the debt fueled decade came crashing down on them resulting in RJR declaring bankruptcy.A fast-paced read and one dominated by investment bankers , it offers a unique insight into the workings and incentives of Wall Street.

"Sal, we gotta go and never stop going till we get there. 
 Where are we going, man? 
 I don't know but we gotta go." 
 I seem to understand why On the Road would polarise opinion because the world is in fact deeply divided.There are those free-spirited souls that believe in chaos and the fact that there is no real goal to life but living and to those , On the Road , would seem almost like a bible of sorts.Sal Paradise is Dante to Dean Moriarty's Virgil as they set off across America to quell that restless madness that seems to afflict them time to time. 
 Others of course would be right to disagree and complain about the fact that there is really no underlying objective or philosophy to their madness.It fact it is to a great extent , a tale of law-breaking , alcohol and drug abuse and mistreatment of women.Yet it endears to wanderers like myself who scoff at the thought of a structured way of life. 
 If you believe that life is about achieving success through a meticulous goal setting program , try another book.This one doesn't have any lessons to teach.

The thing with heralded books on economic thought is that they usually disappoint in terms of the boldness of their analysis and future predictions.Thomas Piketty on the other hand can never be accused of being a pacifist or of anything apart from a radical interpretation of the current economic system. His analysis is exhaustive and extremely well defined in the assumptions he makes.Most eminent economists either applaud or dismiss his school of thought but no on denies that the work is one of the most impressive pieces of scholarship seen in the last decade.A must read for those who wish to ponder on the evolution of the capitalist system.

Bryson is my kind of travel writer.He rarely minces words , uses biting British humour to devastating effect and tells reveal travel secrets worth their weight in gold.His travelogues are the exact antidote to the rosy tripe served up by fawning travel writers with no real appreciation for the best and worst traits observed around Europe.As he says , please leave travel writing to real travellers.

Controversial , exquisite and appalling at the same time , there are few books that will tear your soul apart as Lolita does.How bewitching is Nabokov , that he gets you to pity , hate and feel disgusted all within the same few pages.His dystopian take on love and romance is almost Freudian in it's outlook but does leave you with a real understanding of the complexities of the human psyche.A book in a class of it's own.

Chekov is quite unlike his contemporaries in terms of the setting of his tales and writing style.His prose is lucid , even simplistic, reflective of the characters represented.He is like a painter who doesn't lend much to interpretation but sheds light on the simple pleasures and conflicts that arise throughout life.But as in life , there is meaning in his work , meaning that renders his stories an old world charm,placing him in my humble opinion with in the company of some of the greatest writers in modern literature.

Louis Gerstner masterminded the greatest strategic turnaround at a company long considered as a national treasure.The fact that he did this inspite of a lack of background makes his achievement even more noteworthy.In this book he explains how an integrated system can work if it streamlines it's operations and looks after it's core competencies.He leaves technology companies with a very important lesson-Always put the customer first
An absolute classic written by Hemingway while he was in Havana,Cuba.Reflects his state of mind as he went through a mid life crisis and successful navigated through it
Scary to the core,the book describes how Columbia continues to grapple with civil war as the guerrillas kidnap and ransom a Presidential candidate and her fight for her identity and survival

A master narrator takes you down memory lane, exploring the reasons for India's growth or lack of it since independence through his own experiences as a CEO of a leading multinational and an eminent member of the Indian business community.

A book that will inspire you to dream of changing the world just like Dr Yunus did when he set up a small micro-credit institution in the destitute state of Bangladesh.Pearls of management wisdom from a dreamer who has tackled the problem of poverty in a unique manner and inspired the whole social entrepreneurial movement.
To describe it in one word - awesome.Extremely candid and practical advice on how to maximise return on any scarce commodity and utilize fundamental economics to lead a happier more productive life
Nice book about the positive effects of structured procrastination and how one can channelize this unique trait to work in our favor.
Nice book about a recent idea that has really caught on in the United States.Probably the future of funding which makes it really exciting and an interesting proposition to ponder over

A book with a sense of dark humour that reveals the true reasons for the era of greed that culminated in the greatest depression since the 30s.A first hand account of the fact that human greed and fear remain the only things that drive the financial world.

Lots of negative reviews here. I liked this, perhaps you might to? 
 Background: I've been reading Marvel Comics on and off since I was 10 in 1989. 5 years to begin with, another 5 years or so in 2001 during the Busiek Avengers and Morrison New X-Men runs, then just picking up interesting titles ever since. I'm an old school Marvel zombie, who has read a lot of stories with these characters, and has much affection for Marvel history and the more obscure corners of the MU. 
 I can understand the critique of this series that it doesn't focus so much on the big name core Avengers members. There's lots of brand new characters, and lots of older characters who were never Avengers members. Personally, I have plenty of long boxes full of traditional Avengers comics with the usual members; this served me well as a more experimental title/story. Many of those new members (like Hyperion, Smasher, and Captain Universe) also have ties to the greater MU that was interesting to see tied into the Avengers mythos. It was cool to be able to appreciate some of the easter eggs inherent in the backstories of these characters. And it's not like the old Avenger standby characters were absent by any means. 
 So the story itself was fairly mindbending. Lots of new concepts, a secret history of the universe if you will. It reminded me a lot of Ellis and Cassady's Planetary, in featuring a group of superheroes coming into contact with this secret history/conspiracy. The one off nature of the origin issues of those new members also lent to that Planetary feel, as well as the art. The fights are pretty brutal in the new widescreen style, and I thought Hickman did a good job of setting up a totally strange and unique threat for the team. 
 I can see that this might not be for everyone, but if you're like me, an older fan who has seen a lot, and is interested in an admittedly weird story filled with callbacks, perhaps this will do for you, too.
Beautiful stream of consciousness prose in the early chapters had me very excited, but it degenerates into a very linear and melodramatic plot somewhere around the middle. Ultimately disappointing.

Hizli okunuyor. Merak uyandiriyor ve sizi surukluyor, zaman gecirmek icin okunabilecek bir kitap. Sayfalari cevirirken zamanin nasil gectigini fark etmeyip benim gibi bir gecede okuyabilirsiniz. Fakat benden daha fazla puan alamayacak. (You should know, I don't even like it :P).Biraz acimasiz olacak galiba ama bende karakterler baska genclik romanlarini ve karakterlerini kopyala-yapistir yapmislar gibi bir his birakti. Ugruna onlarca tehlikeye girilen kucuk kardesi ile Penryn'in baglari uzerinde biraz daha durulsa belki farkli bir derinlik yaratilabilirdi. Ayrica ana karakterin pasif kaldigi kisimlardan da hoslanmadim birkac sayfa oncesine donup yazilari degistiresim geldi adeta cunku zamansiz bir pasiflikti. Karakterin tabiri caizse badass kisiliginin bosa gittigini dusundum biraz. Tabi bu benim kisisel fikrim beklentilerim begenen okuyuculardan farkli olabilir. Yine de ilgi cekici bir dunya yaratilmis ve bu dunya surprizler ile dolu bu yuzden okumasi zevkliydi. Ikinci kitabi okumayi dusunuyorum cunku merak ettigim birkac nokta var :)
This book was AMAZING I couldnt put it down, looking forward to the movie

In "Asylum Bound," author Stuart Townsend provides readers with an exceptional picture of what it was and most definitely still is to work and live within the walls of a mental institution. In his 30+ years of working as a nurse at one of Great Britain's oldest institutions he provides some pretty astounding insights at how these establishments work today and gives a nicely detailed history of them to show how they began and how the various treatments started. I will warn you that much of what you have heard of the treatments are very true and this can, at times, be a hard book to read because the author gives you the reality of it. But, if you have any interest in the subject matter then this would be an excellent introduction into the disturbing world of the institution but also the camaraderie of the staff who work there.

Glimpse, the newest offering by author Sara Daniell revolves around Orion Draper, A high school student on a land called the Sphere. When she hears of a strange world called Earth, her questioning nature won't stop until she knows what this "Earth" is all about. Finding her way there is easy but finding her way back home is nearly impossible and life becomes a new danger every second. 
 I think that Sara Daniell has invented an ingenious plot with a cast of very likable characters. Orion is the tough girl who does things by her own rules. Through her rough exterior though she is extremely likable. Her friend Sage is the wonderful comic relief that keeps Orion grounded. Add in Plath, the hunter from the Sphere. He is simply a killer with a heart. The novel is fast-paced with non-stop action. The ending I did not see coming and it definitely makes me eager for the next book in the series.

Love, Amalia is a story of a young Latino girl who is discovering the lessons of loss, friendship and love of family. When this delightful book begins, Amalia is facing a problem with her best friend and shares it with her grandmother. The tender bond and relationship that exists between Amalia and her grandmother is one she will soon understand as she embarks on a journey of self-discovery within life and within herself. 
 The authors, who write from their hearts, do an exceptional job of creating a story that will help parents and caregivers approach the subject of grief and loss with all children. Love, Amalia will also teach the valuable lesson of why people are important and, most importantly, why we ourselves are truly special.

There is much to be said about Tania Ramos' novel, "Be Still." It is a well thought out and well planned novel that actually weaves two interconnecting stories into one. 
 The book revolves around Jack Silver. A father, haunted by the memory of his wife who died somewhat mysteriously many years ago and his son Travis, who has held a long-time grudge against his father, blaming him for his mother's death. Add in the cute Dr. Chris Amity who has been like a daughter to Jack though has always been seen by Travis as somewhat of a leach to his father. However, it will be Travis and Chris who will need to form a bond when tragedy strikes and understand the truths that have been hidden for so long. 
 Over the course of the novel, the author tells a story that blends a mix of inspiration, the afterlife and romance and turns into a convincing tale of redemption. While I did feel that the storyline around Jack became a little tedious and drawn out at times the story surrounding Travis and Chris kept me going on to the end which, while I won't give it away, was a perfect little touch that made me smile. "Be Still" is part medical drama, part romance novel with a hint of "What Dreams May Come." While this genre is not my norm, I did enjoy this very much and recommend it highly.

I have just finished reading When Empires Fall by Katie Jennings and I must say I loved this book! It was a complex and well told story about the Vasser family who has owned a chain of high-end luxury hotels for over 100 years. The family legacy, almost regal in status, begins to crumble after a web of power, deception and murder is unearthed. 
 It is a grand novel in design and there is a lot packed into the 350 plus pages. It is very well written and carefully planned. The thing that pulls you in most of all is the characters that Jennings creates. As she has done in the past she continues to display her knack at character development. In the case of When Empires Fall this makes the story all the more effective yet never confusing. This is a feat that is even more impressive considering there are a lot of characters in this book. From the Scarlett-type Madison and playboy Linc, to the quiet, haunted Grant and charming, bubbly Quinn every character is laid out in a fashion that is believable and real. By novel's end you feel as though you have taken part in the story and have become a family acquaintance. 
 This is a novel that is a must-read and I feel that Katie Jennings is fast-becoming a force to be reckoned with.

There is so much that you can say about how wonderful this book is. I had this as an 11th grade book report and I read it in two days and then read it again. I actually place this in my top five books I've ever read. The story of Bigger Thomas is one that I feel is not only reflective of the time but a little of today as well in the way we view each other. Every scene is so memorable and Richard Wright made his characters so real. It tugged on your emotions at every turn and made you feel like you were part of the story. One fantastic literary achievement.
This was the first Michael Bennett book I have read in the series. I really liked this fast-paced thriller. Looking forward to the other books in the series.

I have been wanting to read this for a long time. I have seen two movie adaptations, the best being "The Innocents" and I was expecting a great an haunting read. However, this book though short, took me forever to read. It just was ok. It was not as good as I had hoped. That said I am glad I did read it but I was hoping for a better read.

Camelot 3000 was one of my favorite comics back in the 80s when it was released and I still love this series today. I know it seems far-fetched, but I always thought the art was wonderful and the story was fantastic! I am a huge King Arthur fan, but usually like it much more close to the original story but I just loved how the characters were incorporated!

Wow! Can't believe all the negative reviews of this. I read this tiny book and really loved it. Yes...it's simple, yes...it's basic common sense, however, as I read it I fit the people in my life into the 4 different characters. The behaviors are very accurate and I have known so many haws that I want to scream! It is a simple story that does have a lot to do with stuff we learned in "The Secret" but is a good refresher to remind you of this common sense approach at life. Cheese is always moving and you adapt or starve.

Katie Jennings debut novel, Breath of Air, is the first novel in the four book Dryad Quartet series and, like its title is a breath of fresh air for the fantasy genre. 
 It revolves around Capri, an orphan girl who, on her 18th birthday discovers the truth of her origins and journeys back to Euphora, the enchanted place where she was born. Soon after Capri returns to Euphora though, strange events begin to happen that mirrors what took place soon before Capri disappeared at the age of three. Capri, her friends and her newfound love begin to unravel the mystery of events both past and present in hopes of bringing peace back to Euphora for good. 
 It is a wonderful first novel for Jennings. Her writing is very descriptive and makes it easy to imagine the world and the characters of Euphora. Speaking of charcters, Jennings give her characters rich histories and interesting personalities. The heroes are very likable and the villains can be quite nasty. Also, there are many characters introduced but I felt that all were developed quite well. 
 It is hard to believe that Breath of Air is Katie Jennings' first novel. The writing is very good, especially for a first novel and she should be commended for undertaking the daunting task of a four book series for her debut works. I am looking forward to the remainder of the Dryad Quartet series as well as future tales from author who looks to have quite a bright future in front of her.

Very good story though a little too short. The characters were very good and I would have liked to seen them fleshed out a bit more but the writer's style is very easy going and easy to read. As I read the story I thought Kendall Lake may have been patterned after Rhett Butler but much nicer. Would have been a 4 if not for the short length and quick rap up. I do recommend it though and look forward to more of Ms. Pape's work.

I loved this book. A fantastic and haunting novella that reminds you of The Picture of Dorian Gray in the style. The book had me on the edge of my seat through the entire story. I am looking forward to more of Mr. Katriel's work. He is a great horror writer who writes like the masters of another time. I even felt a bit of Dickens in his writing. This is a highly suggested read.

As a review for all three parts, I think Odd Interlude was a fun and exciting novella to satisfy us Odd Thomas fans until the release of Odd Apocalypse next month. Not your typical Odd Thomas adventure but a fun read!

I have read many of the early Koontz novels and this is my favorite of those. This has always been one of those I wish he would have decided to update and redo. It is an interesting premise and a well told story.

This was a very early sci-fi novel by Koontz. You could tell he was still finding his voice, but this tale is a fun little romp about a detective that wears a symbiotic apparatus that helps him do his detective work and the werewolf bent on destroying a wealthy and extremely troubled family. It is definitely not up to future Koontz standards, but I enjoyed it nonetheless.

One of the hardest books of Koontz to find, but it is so worth the effort! This is actually one of my all-time favorite books by Koontz. It is a wonderful dark fairy-tale about good toys that are alive and when their creator dies, the bad toys also come to life and seek to destroy the good toys. This is fun, classic and one very enjoyable book with wonderful illustrations by Phil Parks.

This, to me, is one of the greatest graphic novels I have ever read. I have read this and the book. I like this better! To all of you who thought this was based off the Will Smith film it is not. This is based of the original novel and was originally available in the 90s as a four part series. I love the Will Smith film but it only loosely follows the book. The graphic novel has wonderful black and white artwork and is just so well done. If you would like to see a better film adaptation watch "The Last Man on Earth" starring Vincent Price from the late 50s. The Omega Man is also a loose adaptation of the classic tale.

OK...so my wife and I were discussing books and we realized that neither of us had read "Jaws." So we decided to both read it and then watch the film to discuss them both. Well, I am not sure why anyone would have wanted to make this abomination of a book into a film. Thank God that Steven Spielberg did though and that he had the good sense to ditch about 90% of the book's content. 
 This is one of the worst books I have ever read. I am still trying to understand how Peter Benchley ever got a contract? I have read two other of his books and they are all just horrendous. I tried "White Shark" which was beyond bad and "The Island" which I also thought was terrible. 
 Back to "Jaws", The whole side story of Brody's wife was just preposterous and had absolutely nothing to do with the story. In the film she was a minor character and a strong one at that, in the book she is a whiner that Brody should have booted out. Once the affair happened then it was like she was gone? So much about her before and then poof! 
 Honestly, not one character had any redeeming value. I was rooting for the shark to take them all out! 
 I can only imagine the reason this book became so big because it was one of the first book's written about a man-eating Great White Shark. People love sharks and so maybe... 
 If you want a great shark story, Steve Alten's "Meg" series is the way to go. It is far, far better!

OK...this is one of my favorite books of all time! This book had some good frights but it made me laugh! The adventures of Duke and Earl are hilarious. 
 The idea of a nerdy vampire and a redneck werewolf are about as laugh out loud as you can get. It even has a bit of romance. A Lee Martinez has become one of my favorite authors because of this book.
I did like the book. It was extremely slow though. I felt it could have moved along a little faster. I had seen the movie first but really was interested in the book so I read on my Nook.

I have always loved the James Bond novels and truly loved the Raymond Benson Bond novels, so when I saw this offering by Jeffrey Deaver I was intrigued and perplexed. I knew Deaver wrote thrillers, but I wasn't sure he could pull off Bond. I was pleasantly surprised when I finished Carte Blanche. It was a fast-paced, exciting and thoroughly fun Bond adventure. I am hoping that Deaver does another Bond novel and that it will be even half as good as Carte Blanche. Highly recommended!

I have always been a big Raymond Benson fan. I think his James Bond novels are absolutely wonderful so when I picked up his newest book, "The Black Stiletto" I was hopeful that it would be as good as the 007 novels I love so much. Glad to report that his Black Stiletto is an excellent super hero novel. I love that he is now writing the adventures of a super hero. Mr. Benson weaves an exciting and fun story of how the Stiletto comes to be. His characters are well defined and the story comes to an interesting climax. In fact, it made me smile. I am looking forward to further Black Stiletto novels.
One of my all time favorites as a kid and a wonderful, treasured childhood memory. I still remember the doughnut shop story. What a wonderful book for kids of all ages.

This was so much fun! What I thought was really wonderful was how the author truly made the events in the book tie-in with true events and made the entire history seem plausible. Also loved the journal concept. Very well done. Have not yet seen the movie but I must admit I can't wait!

This is one of my all time favorite classic horror thrillers. It remains one of the most chilling and atmospheric stories after all of these years. Watching Dorian's journey from a young naive man into the dark monster he becomes is frightening. It touches on human nature as a whole and the lengths one goes to attain both what they want as well as to feed their fears. Brilliant novel.

I started reading House of Night back in 2009, when I was 17. Never thought I'd still be reading this series seven years later. What a journey. I'll forever cherish theses books because they've been with me for so long. On the other hand, though, they enfuriate me sometimes. Why twelve effing books when you could only do seven (the magic number)? I can't remember what happened in most of them, not because I read them a long time ago but because they were fillers. And not bearable ones. One or two times I considered giving up on this series. But I couldn't. Even though the characters annoyed the hell out of me most of the time and the story kept repeating itself over and over again. I finished them, it's done. I'm saying goodbye to Zoey and her circle and Aphrodite, my forever favourite. But I don't think I'm going to miss them all that much. It's quite sad.
a timeless masterpiece

Never thought I'd dislike this book but... 
 Jane starts as an independent woman and, by the end of the book becomes annoyingly submissive. Don't even get me started on Mr. Rochester. Wow, they do belong together. Two truly awful characters. If you ask me, Bertha Mason was the best one!

** spoiler alert ** 
 I liked it, it's beautifully written. But if I had read it five, four years ago I would'd like it more. It's more for teenagers.
Tao mau que quis chorar por ter perdido o meu tempo a le-lo. O meu primeiro e ultimo livro desta autora.

Lurved it!! 
 I loved all of Lev's quirks and the journey they both took.... But who's story will be next can't wait !!

Heartbreaking Beautiful 
 I loved this book! It was absolutely disturbing and hard to read in places but it was also such a beautiful love story of two people finding themselves in each other..

4 Stars 
 The mystery and the back story were great but who doesn't love a man who knows how to look after his woman, loved Race & Brysen's story.
absolutely heartbreakingly beautiful
Just can't even finish it
4.5 stars

My favourite thing about this book was the use of a child's view to deal with the story of the extermination of the Jewish people by the Nazi regime. The dissassociation used to refer to parts of the story I found astonishing as it helped to get into the story before revealing the centre of the novel. For instance, using 'Out-With' to refer to Auschwitz. 
 On realising the plan of the two little boys I began to predict the ending but I think this made the whole thing more powerful I was willing myself to be wrong. 
 I also adored the way the author joined Bruno and Shmuel together. The two share the same birthday, move somewhere they don't like and look very similar. This really worked to relate the idea that everyone is the same, only the labels people give them are different.
Very unfortunate that these stories are true but a good way to enlighten society to the harm abuse really causes.

This book was amazing cover to cover!! A mix of fantasy, sci fi and dystopian elements, the book followed Darrow as he begins his search for justice. The plot was full of twists, many unpredictable and I loved that about it. I cannot wait to read the next book!!
I really enjoyed this collection of graphic short stories, the art was absolutely beautiful. However not five stars as I didn't enjoy one of the stories as much as the others.

** spoiler alert ** 
 This book was very disappointing. There were many issues with the play. 
 1) The plot was all recycled from the previous novels. We've seen the Triwizard tournament before and been over how Harry's family died before and so on. 
 2) Harry potter books always offered a lesson to readers, and again this play's 'lesson' was one already learnt in Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban. 
 3) Characters were much weaker in comparison to their former selves, especially Ginny. 
 4) Stage directions of heart ache and so on hinted at a homosexual relationship. This would have been nice as the series heavily missed representations of the LGBT community. 
 5) Also, when was Bellatrix supposed to be pregnant? She couldn't have got pregnant before the fourth book as Voldemort did not have corporeal form until the end of this text, and for the fifth, sixth and seventh we see Bellatrix often. Therefore, how was she never seen to be pregnant? 
 I just found the whole thing unnecessary, not very well thought out and annoying as it messed with the past novels. Not a fan.
