When Slim Shady got beat at the Grammy's by Steely Dan two years ago for the Album of the Year, practically everyone under the age of 30 who was watching the telecast knew that the fix had to be in.  "The Marshall Mathers LP" shook the music world to its foundations, making closet fans out of America's suburban youth, sending high-powered politicians into a tizzy, and receiving widespread acclaim in both the mainstream and the underground press.  If "The Marshall Mathers LP" wasn't Album of the Year, it was hard to imagine what it would take for Eminem to overcome the social stigma and finally gain the recognition he deserved.
"The Eminem Show" is here.  And this is what it takes.
After all the hype, after all the controversy, after all the news stories, the hatred, and the doubters, sliding that new full-length Eminem CD into your deck feels like an event.  But truthfully, no adjective could describe how amazing this album truly is.  When you compare this album with the empty, uninspired trash that has made it into heavy rotation since Slim's last release, you quickly realize that despite the offensive nature of some of his sentiments, Marshall Mathers is a genius;  as he dubs himself on "Renegades," a "modern-day Shakespeare."
Eminem is the most gifted poet of our time.  Putting to one side the content of his message, the form of the lyrical structure he creates is unparalleled in the history of hip-hop.  No artist has ever been able to master the intricate rhyme patterns that Eminem seemingly effortlessly spits on song after song after song.  Unlike "The Marshall Mathers LP," in which Slim's lyrical delivery was a bit lacking on a handful of tracks, every single track on "The Eminem Show" features absolute lyrical wizardry from Mathers.  You simply won't believe the verbal gymnastics on the last verse of "Say Goodbye Hollywood," the first verse of "Til I Collapse," the last verse of "Square Dance," just to name a few.  I have been listening to rap and hip-hop for over 15 years, and I personally have never heard anything like this.  As hard as it is to believe, Eminem's style seems to have gotten better since his last release.  Much better.  SCARY better.  I simply don't think there is currently another commercial rapper alive who can compete with this.  Eminem is so much better than his contemporaries at his delivery that he makes heavy hitters like Jay-Z and Nas look like amateurs.  I mean no disrespect to Jay-Z and Nas whatsoever.  I have every one of their albums, I love them both to death, but Eminem is just leaps and bounds better than them.  It's almost funny how good he is.
Turning to the content of the album, I was surprised and delighted to find that Eminem has almost completely abandoned his tactic of dissing Britney, Christina Aguilera, and N-Sync.  Aside from the Moby reference on the single, "Without Me," a few Canibus slams on "Square Dance," and a Jermaine Dupri double-team with Dr. Dre on "Say What You Say," Eminem has shied away from using his lethal lyrics to assault and batter his peers in the music industry.  This is refreshing, because Eminem's talent is so profound that for him to even acknowledge the existence of the Britneys and N-Syncs only reduces his credibility.  What remains of Em's anger on the new album is primarily directed towards the father who abandoned him, the girlfriend who betrayed him, the media that alienates him, the politicians that censor him, the millions of parents that blame him, and, of course, his mother, who Eminem pinpoints as the source of his neverending animosity and rage.  While the lyrics on "The Marshall Mathers LP" aimed to shock and insult, many of the words on this album are devoted to social commentary and, believe it or not, political statement.  I found myself frequently nodding in agreement along with "White America," which provides a four-minute glimpse into the truth behind Eminem's rapid rise to stardom, "Square Dance," which contains some thinly-veiled antiwar messages, and "Sing For The Moment," which samples Aerosmith's "Dream On" and will bring a tear to your eye if you aren't careful.
Following along with the title of the album, Eminem also talks alot about himself.  In "Cleaning Out My Closet," he savages his mother worse than ever before, and gives listeners some insight into his childhood.  In "Say Goodbye Hollywood," my early pick for the album's best song, he opines about the downside of fame. (Incidentally, this song serves as a nice bookend to "The Slim Shady LP"s "If I Had," which features Em pining for more fame.  Be careful what you wish for...)  And finally, on "Hailie's Song," Em offers a touching tribute to his daughter.  Although he makes a failed attempt at singing on this track--one of his few missteps on the album--when the "real" Slim Shady triumphantly returns on the song's last verse with another stellar rap verse, you're inclined to almost immediately forgive him.  And it's nowhere near as bad as Biggie on "Playa Hata."
The year isn't over yet, but "The Eminem Show" is a safe bet for the year's best.  Eminem is today's version of The Beatles;  not in terms of the style or content of his music, but in terms of his effect on the culture and the minds of America's youth.  Eminem proudly represents the conflict inside each and every one of us.  The struggle between doing right and doing wrong; between maturity and immaturity;  between genius and insanity.
But he probably still won't win the Grammy.
Dan

With all the press and scrutiny that Marshall "Eminem" Mathers
gets,you can't help but be  bombarded with his overly publicized,scrutized very public profile. After becoming a househould name and the (mostly white)
press' poster boy for "bad behavior" with his multi-platinum 2000 opus "The Marshall Mathers LP",Eminem comes back to stir up more "controversy" with his followup,"The Eminem Show".
Now I know that surburban kids and even many real hip hop heads are going to applaud this album but the real deal with "The Eminem Show" is that it's no real "Show"-stopper...
This album is rather dull,predictable,and redundant. Never have I seen a hardcore hip hop album so blantantly targeted to white,
surburban youth. It doesn't take a rocket scientist to see what Eminem's formula is:spit raunchy,"shocking" rhymes over slow,
menacing beats that give kids in the "boondocks" a taste of the thug life and mischievous excitement that they so crave and then whine about how bad your life is.
That's the basic formula and "The Eminem Show" milks it for all it's worth.
Eminem tries to play with the issues of race and the government
on this 77 minute opus' opener "White America",spitting rhymes that claim that his white skin color was the real reason for his MTV success and that the government just wants to blame him for society's problems. Good premise but Eminem sounds so dim and harried that his point never leaves the ground and "America" comes off flat and as yet another attempt to shock.
Obligatory "I hate my life"-styled tracks like "Cleanin' Out My Closet" and the perky,Dr. Dre-produced "Business" will get the "TRL" crowd cheering but won't do anything for real music heads,if you ask me.
Now I'll give Eminem props by saying that "Show" is very well-produced but what's the point when the rhymes are so redundant
and so forced. The misogynistic sex rap "Superman" sounds very odd coming from a man who once rhymed that he wanted to slaughter his wife now boasting about his prowess with the females. And the unattractive sex rap "Drips" is just simply another boring turn-off.
Trudging cuts like "Till I Collaspe" and the Dre-produced Jermaine Durpri diss "Say What You Say" also make you want to get a pillow and call it a night because this has been done so many times before by him.
(I won't even mention the unabashed MTV-aimed first single
"Without Me":Is it me or does it sound like he's rapping over bad club music?)
So yes,that's the deal,Mr. Mathers is out to swear his way to the bank(which he's already done,considering that this album sold a million copies in it's first full week of release) and unnerve the establishment but instead in reality,"The Eminem Show" is basically a stale,repetitive,un-shocking bore.

On his third commercially released album, Eminem is at his most personal... He talks about many things and people in many different ways... On the track "Cleanin Out My Closet" he talks to his mum. Someone who he obviously cares for, but at the same time has hate for, "Cleanin Out My Closet" was produced by Eminem himself and a very eerie beat is what he concocts, it goes perfect with his flow... Another one of the many 'personal' tracks on the LP is "White America" a rock influenced aggressive song taking shots at the U.S government amongst other things. Like quite a large amount of songs on this album this track has a sort of "rock / rap" feel about it.. Eminem's lyrics & flow are incredible here. "Business" is one of the few Dr. Dre produced cuts on the album, and this track wouldn't be out of place on Eminem's debut commercial album [The Slim Shady LP].. It features the return of Slim Shady the commedian, and also has Dre's best beat on the whole album. A standout track is "Sing For The Moment" this song samples the classic rock track "Dream On" by Aerosmith.. Eminem spits three of his hottest verses ever, very politcal and consciensus Hip Hop on this track right here... Another track worth mentioning is "Say What You Say" which features Dr. Dre - who also produces this song - Although I don't personally like the song, The 2 rapppers take shots at commercial Producer/Rapper/Executive Jermaine Dupri..
The album isn't very guest filled, but the rest of D12 step-up their game on "When The Music Stops" a great track about the thin-line between music and reality... New Shady Records signee and Detroit based MC Obie Trice appears on the comic "Drips" a great verse by Obie followed by an -as always- excellent verse by Slim ensue one of the my fave songs on the album...
What some may find about The Eminem Show is that the production doesn't stand-out, It just plays along in the background backing up Eminem's venemous words...3 Tracks are produced by west-coast super producer Dr. Dre and the rest are produced by Eminem, with a little help from others [Mel - Man etc]...
So, overall an incredible album from Eminem which is very personal and should definetly appeal to the hardcore rap fans, as well as the 11/12 year old's...
Final Rating: 9/10

Marshall Mathers showed up unexpected in 1999 with his first taste of success, the annoying single "My Name Is". The white rapper made toes cringe, mouths drop & tempers flair as he sold millions after millions of copies. Openly bashing gays, lesbians, and numerous different races and cultural groups Eminem took the entire world by storm, selling a staggering 20 million copies in just 4 short years. He has captivated the entire music industry and countless depressed young american teens that were feeling what he was saying and looking for a way out.
I can honestly admitt, I hated Eminem. Though I'm not gay, jewish or a lesbian, I felt bad for these groups of people because he was making them feel terrible about their lifestyles. His lyrical content was terrible, it was all comical & fictional and he never really discussed the problems that surronded him everyday. But Eminem surprised millions, when he dropped -=The Eminem Show=- an emotionally deep and surprising release which dealt with his insecurities, family problems, life in the lime light and the demons that constantly surrond him, which makes out for his best material.
The Nate Dogg laced "Till I Colapse" is easily the albums best track. With Eminem dropping his clever trademark lyrics over a "get-up-and-dance beat", the song is guarrenteed to be a smash. His wordplay on "Without Me" is welcomed as well, and is another party track that easily out does his previous singles, which lacked substance and direction. But these songs are ones that you would expect on an Eminem album, its the "out of place" tracks that really allow Marshall to shine.
"Hallies Song" a track where Eminem flexes his singing talents is absolutely amazing. The track is so personal and Eminem really surprises me with this lyrics which are hand written beautifully. Another surprise track was "Cleaning out my Closet" where he finally confronts the issues with his mother and explains why he has reacted the way he did. He also talks about Kim without going down is imaginative psychotic path and just sticking to the facts.
With Britney & Christina bashing aside, Marshall Mathers has been able to step outside his role as america's most hated white bred, and speak out about the issues that have plagued his career since he first grabbed the microphone on his first album. (Considering "The Slim Shady LP" the first because the underground albums weren't nationally released.) I am proud of Eminem for doing this album, and can say that he really shut me up. The album's a surprisingly progressive step for someone from whom so little was expected.

Eminem is -- in his way -- and imaginative and engaging rapper, and his last two albums were highly inspired and chock-full of viscious energy. Production was solid and clean but usually nicely restrained and minimal (see "My Name Is" and "Kill You.") Neither the Slim Shady LP nor the Marshall Mathers LP were "pure genius," but they were certainly good records.
The Eminem Show has its moments, but overall, is a definite step down. First of all, his lyrical flow (which he mentions often with pride) seems a bit stunted and clumsy on a lot of this material. The legato pacing is the same on almost every track and the wording is sometimes awkward and ineffective. The content is often boring. Eminem seems to be taking himself a lot more seriously on this record, addressing "big issues," unnecessarily and unentertainingly. The first track is a good example. It's incredibly high-school in its petulant anti-authoritarian posturing. He actually uses the phrase "democracy of hypocrisy" ... ! What is this, a Rage Against the Machine record? When he's not taking unclever jabs at "the system," he's still whining about his mother, all that horrible money and fame which just makes him SOOO miserable, and women. The notable addition to the content this time around is that he yatters on about how much he loves his daughter, like a giddy soccer mom. Just get a bumper sticker and be done with it. I'm sure all the Backstreet Boys fans and other teeny-bopper MTV girls out there will find it just ADORABLE, especially when he actually SINGS on "Hailie's Song" -- sounding every bit like a wannabe member of 'N Sync, a band he's often attacked and ridiculed in the past.
Many of the tracks here are simply boring, with a lackluster flow and nothing to really grab your interest. I kept waiting for something to happen on this record, something to really grab me, make me laugh, etc. Eminem's always been good at commanding the listener's attention -- not so much here. I was tuning in and out by the third or fourth track. Halfway through each song I was simply waiting for it to end, hoping the NEXT one would be one of the really good ones.
Production: the production on this album is irritatingly commercial, and commercial in a poor way. I agree with the reviewer who criticized the choruses. Boring and long and overproduced, sounding like just about everything else the mainstream music industry pumps out. They repeat themselves in exactly the same fashion at the designated places; almost every song is structured in a completely predictable and formulaic fashion. After twenty tracks it gets old.
The skits are dumb. I've never been a huge fan of the skit thing, but these are worse than usual. They're just uninspired.
With all that said, rest assured there ARE a few decent tracks and memorable moments. "Drips" is amusing, and "Soldier" would be an excellent track if it weren't for the cheesy melodramatic atmosphere of it, (particularly the chorus.) "Cleaning Out My Closet" isn't too bad, (though it's more whining about his mom), and "Sing for the Moment" is well executed, (though again, far too dramatically serious.) Don't get me wrong -- a somber track here and there is OK, but this album in general completely lacks a sense of humor, and a sense of playfulness. The exception is the single, "Without Me," which is pretty classic light-hearted Eminem, viscious and whimsical at the same time. It is not reminiscent of the rest of the disc at all I'm afraid.
Overall Eminem's material is becoming less like fun, outrageous, in-your-face rap, and more like a whiney extended public therapy session. He's not controversial anymore; he just TALKS about how controversial he has been in the past. (Yawn.) I think this could be a sort of transitional record -- cleaning up after the Marshall Mathers LP, so to speak, closing the book on his mom, Kim, cementing his feelings about his daughter and his own press, etc. If so, fine: I hope he's now gotten it out of his system and will move on come the next release.

Eminem's third album, The Eminem Show, lacks the amazing tracks of the Marshall Mathers LP, such as "Marshall Mathers," "Criminal," and "Stan." However, this album is by far the MC's most consistent and actually  is the second best of his three albums.  The smash single "Without Me" is the most radio friendly track, while "Say What You Say" featuring Dr. Dre is an excellent response to Jermaine Dupri's boasting. "Cleanin' Out My Closet" and "White America," though, are the album's two standout tracks. The former song puts an end to Eminem's feud with his mother Debbie Mathers, while the latter is a brilliant (and incredibly harsh) diatribe insulting American stereotypes and advocates of censorship such as Lynne Cheney and Tipper Gore. All in all, the album is well worth the price becuase of its incredible consistency-- THERE ARE NO BAD SONGS ON THIS ALBUM.

I'll be the first to admit that it took a while for me to catch on to Eminem.  When I first heard his "Slim Shady LP", I thought it was good for some laughs but was hard to take seriously.  When the "Marshall Matthers LP" came out I felt otherwise.  I had heard Eminem on a few tracks off of Dr. Dre's "Chronic 2001" and the "Matthers LP" and I heard frustration and humor that puts a lot of rap artists to shame.  He's a rare talent that isn't afraid to take shots at people.  His lyrics are shocking and filled to the brim with four letter words but he puts his heart into his music I believe.  I can't say I approve of everything he says or would support parents buying his albums for young children but on his latest CD, he is in top form.
  "The Eminem Show" has some of the best music Eminem has ever recorded.  "Without Me" is the single that is being pushed on the radio and MTV but that song is sandwitched in between songs with much deeper and personal lyrics.  "Cleanin Out My Closet" finds Eminem at his most reflective and I can't imagine he'll ever do a song that tops it.  Dr. Dre (producer) samples lyrics and music from Aerosmith's "Dream On" on "Sing for the Moment".  I can see the two groups on stage now performing this track.  Many guests such as Dre and D-12 (a group of rappers that Eminem produced on their first album, "Devil's Night") make vocal appearances.
  I think Eminem has managed to make more enemies than friends over the last few years but he comes out on top in the end, like it or not.  I do not agree with a lot that he has to say sometimes, but to not recognize his talent and his creativity isn't fair.  He turns frustration into art and not everyone can do that.  With his deep lyrics and Dr. Dre's solid production, "The Eminem Show" is a five star record and Eminem's finest to date.

Marshall "Eminem" Mathers took the world by storm once his single "My Name Is" was released.  Some people looked at his style as eerie and twisted humor and others actually realized that he had skills.  Whatever the formula, people ate it up real quick and Eminem soon became a household name.  Yes, some of the press was from his controversial lyrics, but at the same time, his distinct style created a path for him to remain an artist for years to come.  On his 2nd disc, "The Marshall Mathers LP", Eminem definitely put himself on the map.  His 1st single "The Real Slim Shady" only created a small path for the CD's better songs like "The Way I Am", "I'm Back", "B Please 2", "Kill You", "Who Knew" and the CD's smash hit, "Stan" w/Dido.  After selling 1.7 million units in the 1st week of sales, no one could deny Eminem of his "status".  Many social groups came to speak out about his controversial lyrics and the haters were everywhere but that only made more people buy the CD.  That's what a lot of people that don't deal with music don't understand.  More press just adds to better record sales.  Before his 3rd disc was released, Eminem's group, D12, would go on to release a CD and because of the success of the singles "Purple Pills" and "Fight Music" the CD went on to go platinum.  He also appeared on and produced the song "Renagade" that was on Jay Z's "Blueprint" CD.  On his 3rd disc, "The Eminem Show", Eminem's displays a lot of the antics that he did on his previous 2 CDs.  However, this time is seems that Mr. Mathers is more about his business.  The songs aren't as playful as the songs on "The Marshall Mathers LP.  "White America" starts the CD off in pure Eminem fashion.  He plays off of the irony on how he has been successful in a world that he is not set up to be successful in.  Check the chorus out..  "I could be one of your kids", "Little Eric could look like this", "Erica loves my s...", I go to TRL, look how many hugs I get".  He sceams the words "White America" between each line.  The first single, "Without Me", does the same thing that "The Real Slim Shady" did for "The Marshall Mathers LP".  It's not one of "The Eminem Show's" better songs but it gets the listener's attention enough to make you want to buy the CD.  The CD's best song in my opinion is definitely "Cleanin' Out My Closet".  This song allows Eminem to tell his side of the story about everything that has gone on between him and his mom.  It's as honest as he can get and his fans should be able to appreciate this track.  "I'm sorry Mama, I never meant to hurt you, I never meant to make you cry, but tonight I'm cleanin' out my closet".  This songs also allows you to see how everyday life is seen through Eminem's eyes.  The production is handled primarily by Eminem himself.  Dr. Dre produces 3 songs: "Business", "My Dad's Gone Crazy" w/Eminem's own daughter Hailie Jade and "Say What You Say", where Eminem and Dr. Dre rip "Mini-Me" (Jermaine Dupri) apart with each line.  Other noteworthy songs include "Square Dance", "When The Music Stops" w/D 12, "Sing For The Moment" and "Drips" w/Obie Trice from D 12.  This CD definitely displays Eminem's versatility.  Overall, any fan of Eminem's previous 2 CDs will enjoy "The Eminem Show".  It is definitely worth the price of admission.

Welcome home, Em. He's been gone for a while. "No he hasn't", you say, "he's released the Marshall Mathers LP in 2000 and the D-12 album last year" (don't admit that you actually bought that D-12 album, by the way). But true underground heads know that he took a vacation from the streets and started kicking some Generation-X, MTV-ready raps for all of America to eat up and/or criticize. But just like Jay-Z did with The Blueprint and Nas did with Stillmatic, Eminem brings it back to the streets with his third album, The Eminem Show. There's not one commercial, radio-friendly song on this album (except for "Without Me", which is the weakest track on here compared to the rest of the songs). Forget the title to the first single off his second album, THIS is the Real Slim Shady.
If you think he has totally ditched his style (shock value lyrics, dissing your favorite artists for no reason), you're wrong, as evidenced on "Without Me"'s third verse when he disses an *NSYNC member and Moby. The beef continues on "Say What You Say" when guest Dr. Dre takes shots at a certain producer in Atlanta: "I'm a giant...when I see you I'ma step on you and not even know it/You midget/...Over eighty million records sold/And I ain't have to do it with 10- or 11-year-olds." Timbaland also puts his two cents in as well at the end of the track. Unfortunately, we heard all this dissing before (The Roots vs. Nas, Nas vs. Jay-Z, Jay-Z vs. anybody who ain't him) so you're left with a "Who cares?" feeling. Therefore, the diss records (with artists) thankfully stop there.
Eminem, still one of the best, if not THE best, rapper in the game, brings it on politically ("White America"), explains his reasoning for him hating his parents ("Cleaning Out My Closet"), and shows affection for the only female he loves: his daughter ("Hailie's Song"). And songs like "Say Goodbye Hollywood" talk about his recent lawsuit(s). Now I wouldn't dare rank Eminem with 2Pac, but just like Pac's Me Against the World versus his other albums, The Eminem Show is Em's darkest and most personal record, which is why it's his best album.
Dudes on the block will be arguing over what's the best song on the album, but my pick is "When the Music Stops" with D-12, where, for once, everyone sounds good. And "Soldier" and "Till I Collapse" tie at second. In fact, there's not one song worth skipping on this album, but the aforementioned "Without Me", which really sounds like "The Real Slim Shady Part 2", comes close.
You either like Eminem or you don't, and he's not gonna change for no one. Like he said a few years back, he just don't give a you-know-what. But those who think that Eminem has changed his style are just mad because they can't find the "hits" that they found on his last two albums. This album is for the true Eminem fans only, not the mainstream, current-fad loving, bandwagon-jumping individuals. You probably won't see another single off this album on TRL, so that means that most of his fans will throw this album away. Oh well, their loss.

The lyrics are clever and intellegent, and for the most part don't rely on ... tricks and shock value. I was very, very pleasantly surprised. Each song is atleast pretty good on this CD, and it is EASILY better than all his other CDs. Heres my lowdown of the tracks.
------------------------
-1. Curtains Up (skit)- 0/5 - Its an intro...what can I say, I'm not a fan of intros and skits.
-2. White America- 5/5 - This is the track the convinced me I was in head for an amazing album. The beat, the lyrics and the over all composure of this track is beautiful.
-3. Business- 4/5 - After the first song, this song is a great way to lighten you up. Its less serious, and more fun (I love the Andre and Rapboy bit...) However, the repeated "Marshall!" got to me after awhile.
-4. Cleaning Out My Closet- 5/5 - Another track on this CD is absolutely love. I can listen to this track forever. The only weak point I find on this track is the first verse starts off pretty monotone and boring. However, it picks up into a serious and well scripted telling of his life.
-5. Square Dance- 5/5 - And another comedic track to break from the serious. This track has an awesome beat, and I love the lyrics. The chorus is awesome too, and sounds really neat.
-6. The Kiss (skit)- 3/5- 3/5 is an EXTREMELY high mark for a skit to recieve with me. However, this skit has a great mood set with the dramatic music in the background. It is also the most serious, and most meaningful skit I have ever listened to.
-7. Soldier- 4/5- Soldier is an okay song, with a good beat and fairly good lyrics, but it falls short compared to the other stuff.
-8. Say Goodbye Hollywood- 5/5- Another one of my favourite songs on this CD. The chorus, the lyrics, the story. Its like a perfect display of events explaining his life and position...brings a tear to your eye.
-9. Drips - 4/5- Drips has one of my favourite choruses on the CD, and the message is good...I think. It has a good beat as well, and gives you a good taste of whats gonna come from Obie.
-10. Without Me- 3/5- Without Me is probably one of my least favourite songs on the CD...although I still enjoy it. It is a good party song, but Is the new "Real Slim Shady" (thats to say its good...until you hear it too many times)
-11. Paul Rosenberg- 1/5- Another boring skit...
-12. Sing For The Moment- 4/5- I like this song...especially the melodic chorus. Its a good song, and shows his artistic growth.
-13. Superman- 6/5- I LOVE this songs chorus. The chorus of this song is amazing, and the verses don't fall short either. This is my favourite track on the CD, easily.
-14. Hailie's Song- 3/5- EMINEM's attempt at singing isn't the greatest, but I actually like this song. Especially the fact he acknowledges he can't sing, and only is singing for his girl.
-15. Steve Berman- 2/5- Another Skit...It got such a "high" mark because I like Steve.
-16. When the Music Stops- 4/5- -This song gives some of the variety that makes this CD so great. I like some of D12s stuff (Especially stuff like "I'll Sh*t On You"
-17. Say What You Say- 4/5- Yet another good track..but you probably saw that coming. He teams up with mentor Dr. Dre for this track, and this track helps remind us how em got big in the first place.
-18. 'Till I Collapse- 4/5- Another song I really like, although just for the chorus more than anything else. Nate Dogg was very well picked for the part of this song's chorus.
-19. My Dad's Gone Crazy- 5/5- I love this song. The lyrics are a little iffy, but thats because the song is about him...well... going crazy. Hailie is perfect in this song too, making it an awesome chorus. The only thing I really don't like in this song is Hailie's creepy laugh at the end...
-20. Curtains Close- 3/5- What can I say...Its a skit yes, but there is singing making fun of the worst song on this CD...

Love him or hate him, you have to agree that Eminem is one hell of a lyricist.  Beyond his boyish looks and skin color, he is one of the most popular rappers to embrace the rap scene in a long time.  Despite all the critics, protesters, and uptight politicians who would like nothing more but for this man to never speak again, with his third album "The Eminem Show," Eminem has crafted a magnificent album that will have you hooked from the very first track.
Though he is well known for his edginess and controversial image on "The Marshall Mathers LP," this album proves to be Eminem's most personal and honest work.  The songs also are a lot more catchier and well-constructed in my opinion.  And he doesn't wait to let out his aggressions on his critics and protesters.  He digs right in with a song called, "white america," where in the chorus he repeats, "I could be one of your kids / little Eric looks just like this."  He goes more deeper into his problems with his estranged mother in the song, "cleanin out my closet."  And although this album is his most personal and serious, don't think that his enemies aren't going to get attacked by this lyricist.  From Cannabis in "square dance," to Limp Bizkit and Moby in "without me," Eminem dishes out a full-blown attack on anyone who opens their mouth about him.  And those are only some of the songs on the album I have mentioned.
His most personal song would have to be "Hailey's song," which is a tribute to his daughter.  He even goes as far as to sing through most of it.  Who would've thought, Slim Shady himself can actually sing.  He doesn't do a bad job, at that.  Still, I think he shouldn't quit with the rapping.
Don't worry.  Although this album isn't as edgy or frightening as "The Marshall Mathers LP," there are still plenty of humorous verses and choruses, filled with disses and venom.  And there are still going to be moments where you will be listening with your jaw on the floor thinking to yourself, "He didn't just say what I think he said!"  Eminem still is able to catch us off guard and make us cringe at times, but he's just saying what's on his mind.  I think his most outrageous song on the album is, "my dad's gone crazy," which features his daughter.  If his mother thought he did a number on her on "The Marshall Mathers LP," it's nothing compared to what he says in this song!
I really enjoyed this album, and right now I'm hooked on it.  I can't stop listening to it.  I loved every song, with the exception of "drips."  I don't hate the song, it's just not one of my favorites.  My favorite songs are, "white america," "without me," "sing for the moment," "my dad's gone crazy," and "square dance."  I really believe that if you're a true Eminem fan, you will love this CD.  It's still has edge to it and it is in no way watered down.  Eminem has a talent and I hope he keeps rapping for a long time.

Emienem's junior effort is hot.  His creative word play is untouchable.  It's no holds barred.  I see why people were rushing to get the copy off the internet. He also displays his feelings on his failed marriage, his severed relationship with his mother, and his undying love for his daughter. You can hear the pain & anger towards his mother on "Cleaning out my Closet".  This song made me truly appreciate my relationship with my mother.  The love for his daughter can be felt in "Hailie's Song".  His attempt to sing this for her shows his gentle parental side.  You can hear throughout several songs that he adores Hailie.  She's the reason for getting in the rap game.  In "Say Goodbye to Hollywood," he says "All I wanted was to give Hailie the things I never had, instead I forced us to live alienated".  Living in Detroit, Em was on the evening news every week last summer because the nightclub incident.  There were several stories reported about his and Kim's marriage.  I don't know if it made national news, but the news reported that Kim tried to commit suicide.  He did try to make his marriage work for the sake of his daughter. The Detroit news was practically Court TV.
This CD is not as commercial as the Marshall Mathers LP, but will be as successful.  "White America" is straight to the point.  It doesn't matter if he's white in the Hip Hop community because he's got skills, but it really helped his record sales.  He wouldn't have sold as much or be able to get away half the things he says if he was black, but that's how the music industry works.
Eminem's "Superman" sounds like it was following the lead of LL Cool J's "I Need Love" until the last line of the chorus.  Groupies Beware!!!  "Drips" is safe sex message by storytelling without preaching.  He and D-12 sarcastically rap about how society say Hip Hop music has influenced the behavior of the youth on "When the Music Stops".  "Say What You Say" is classic Eminem.  He and Dre blast on little Papa Smurf J.D.  The final song is "My Dad's Gone Crazy" with Hailie making her recording debut.  The DVD is 45 minutes worth of concert clips, interviews, and an episode of his animated show, Slim Shady.
All in all, this is a must buy.  This is his most artistic effort to date.  He strips away layers of complexity song after song. I can't wait to 8 Mile this summer/fall.  The part of the movie was made near my neighborhood.  The production was crew was really nice.  They let me watch them film a few scenes.

And here it is...the long awaited follow up to The Marshall Mather LP, and does it live up to it's hype? well, sort of. This is somewhat of a topsy-turvy record that has it's great points and it's not so great points. First off, let me say that the "skits" on the cd are terrible. Just plain terrible. Obviously not thought out at all and thrown together, sloppily. But you don't buy the cd for the skits right? Here is a rundown of the songs: (5 stars being the best, 1 the worst)
White America: A great song with a good beat. An excellent rap by Eminem and some thought provoking lyrics. 3 1/2 stars
Business: One of the best songs on the record. A great catchy beat and chorus and some excellent raps to boot. 4 1/2 stars
Cleaning Out My Closet: An emotional trip through eminem's life. Very well rapped and a great beat. Another one of the best songs on the record. 4 stars
Square Dance: By far, the worst song on the record. This song feels very sloppy and rushed. Not very catchy at all and the raps are sub-par for slim. 1 star
Soldier: A great song. Emotional and solid. Great raps and an overall great feel to it. 4 stars
Say Goodbye Hollywood: A very different song for eminem. Exploring some other aspects of hip hop here. Comes off a bit weird but good none-the-less. 3 1/2 stars
Drips: Probably the second worst song on the album. Sloppy. 1 1/2 stars
Without Me: Probably the best song on the record overall. (I guess that's why he released it as his first single off it) Fantastic beats, outstanding raps, a great song. 4 1/2 stars
Sing for the Moment: A very interesting twist on the "Aerosmith" song Dream On. Eminem has some solid raps in this one and the beat is great for the verses. I think the song loses a little bit in the chorus, but overall, a good song with some meaningful lyrics. 4 stars
Superman: I am editing my opinion of this song because it has grown on me in a huge way. I now can't stop listening to it. 4 stars.
Hailie's Song: This is a great song except for the fact that eminem can't sing. (He says he can't in the song) but that doesn't take away from the fact that he really can't sing. at all. The song has a nice beat and the lyrics are emotional, but overall, not nearly his best effort. 3 stars
When the Music Stops: An overall good song with some guest appearences (namely, Bizarre from D12) Some good raps and a solid beat. 3 1/2 stars
Say What You Say: Now here is my biggest disappointment with the record. I was looking forward to this song a lot when I found out that Dre was going to be rapping on it and the fact that it was going to be a JD diss (I hate JD)but this song just comes up short. The beat is choppy and rushed and em's and Dre's raps could be much better. Not terrible but nowhere near great. 2 1/2 stars
Till I Collapse: One of my favorite songs on the album. It has a "We will Rock You" feel to it but comes off sounding good. Em has some solid raps and the overall feel of the song is solid. 4 stars
My Dad's Gone Crazy: Wacky! This song is pretty funny with Eminem's Daughter (I assume it's em's daughter, I could be wrong)providing the chorus. It sounds crazy but grows on you, and the rest of the track is solid. 4 stars
Well, that's my rundown of the "Eminem Show" Overall I would say that's it's a good record but not as good as "The Marshall Mathers LP"

Yes, that annoying blonde motormouth has returned. If it seems that he's still rapping about the same stuff (hating his mom and Kim, loving his daughter, dissing his fans and his detractors), you're pretty close. However, he has dropped a few nuggets of political wisdom within the album ("White America", "Squaredance") and his flows (especially about current pop culture) still astound. On top of that, he's produced most of the album, which is a good thing because he's learned some tricks and keeps the sounds interesting if the rap drags, throwing in a club beat ("Without Me"), Southern bounce ("Squaredance"), upper-class rap-rock ("White America") and funk ("Till I Collapse"). In spite of a simply horrible, misogynistic duet with Obie Trice that is completely unnecessary ("Drips"), this album captures the three-faced persona of Marshall Mathers (the loving, yet narcisstic human), Eminem (Marshall's rap persona who is arrested and has a hot temper) and Slim Shady (Eminem's further ego who is plain twisted) in the most complete way yet. If some of the fat of this album was cut and the personas a little more concentrated and focused, this album would have been a sheer masterpiece. However, it's light years ahead of most third albums in an artist's career, let alone in rap. He's still the most compelling artist since Kurt Cobain and most vital of today. Let the "Show" begin.

Yes, Eminem delivers again in his newest masterpiece, The Eminem Show.

Without Me follows Drips and it is the hit single of the CD. Without Me is a music video on MTV, and the most popular song on The Eminem Show. Still, I'll give it 4 out of 5 stars for its somewhat limited lyrics, althought I love the Moby and N'Sync bashing.
Sing for the Moment is a cover of Aerosmith's Dream On smash hit, with Tyler singing the chorus. Brilliant cover, incredible lyrics, one of the best songs of Eminem's career. Easily gets a 5/5.
Superman is more hip-hopish and explains Eminem's dating life to a certain extent. Great beat, good lyrics...5/5.
Halie's Song is kind of a dare I say it, popish song but sounds very good coming from Eminem. The kid can sing though as he proves it tonight. Great song, catchiest on the album, 5/5.
When the Music Stops features D12 singing on it, decent lyrics, solid beat...4/5.
Say What U Say features Dre and is an overall good song...4/5.
Till I Collaspe is a weaker song on the album, but still good...it has Nate Dogg on it, and gets 3/5.
The last song is My Dad's Gone Crazy with Eminem's daughter, Hailie Jade singing some. 4/5, cute song, pretty clever stuff.

The Eminem Show in a word is Awesome. Who can deny Slim Shady of extremely good lyrical skills? No one. From the minute people heard of the completion of this LP, they knew this was THE album to get this spring/summer. That's what we have all come to love about Marshall Mathers. When he drops a CD, we know it's satisfaction guaranteed. How many artists can give us that feeling nowadays? Only a handful or maybe even less. And without a single doubt, Eminem is one of those artists.
From the beginning, on "White America", which by the way, is the albums highlight, we all get that refreshing feeling that we are blessed to hear arguably the top hip-hop artist of today on some much needed good music. This song is what Eminem is all about. Displaying his lyrics like no other rapper and telling us what we want to hear, his inner most feelings.
"Business" is a hit we can all enjoy with hip-hop's top producer on the beats. Witty, funny, creative lyrics over a tight Andre Young beat. Eminem's Batman to his Robin. Arguably the best one-two punch in hip-hop history. The track that follows, "Cleaning Out My Closet", is the second best track as we hear Marshall dishing out his most personal feelings to date over a beat. "Square Dance" is sure to create yet another beef in the rap game. This time it's Slim Shady himself versus Canibus. Many people had doubted Eminem's guts as he only dissed pop acts. But now, he has officially dissed a rapper. A black rapper. We shall see how Canibus responds. Canabis is not going to let this slide. That's a guarantee. Marshall is upset at Canabis because Canabis used Em's character from his Marshall Mathers LP, Stan, to his benefit on his [wack] album, C True Hollywood Stories.
Other slammin' tracks include his lead single, "Without Me", which needs no explanation since everyone has heard it by this time. It's not possible to review this CD and not mention Eminem's singing, yes, SINGING, on a tribute to his daughter, "Hailie's Song". No, Slim is not a good singer, yet the track comes out smooth and lovely. "Say What You Say" finds Eminem playing Dr. Dre's devils advocate on a diss song aimed a hip-hop producer/rapper, Jermaine Dupri. It's a classic diss song. The content of this song stems from Jermaine Dupri stating that he (himself) is hip-hop's untouchable top producer. A statement Dre and Timbaland (Extravagant hip-hop producer) didn't take lightly. It was a sign of disrespect.
Rounding out the album is "'Till I Collapse" featuring the lovable Nate Dogg. Using a beat similar to Queens "We Will Rock You", Em is again on top of his game. Marshall mentions other rappers that he has the utmost respect for (Reggie [Redman], Jay-Z, 2pac, Biggie, Andre from OutKast, Jadakiss, Kurupt and Nas). Can't argue with that! "My Dad's Gone Crazy" features none other than Eminem's own daughter, the cute Hailie Jade playfully stating that her dad is crazy. Over a hot Dr. Dre beat, this one is a dope song.
Now comes the bad. "Drips" featuring the Shady Record's own, Obie Trice, is not that great. It sounds like something out of the Slim Shady LP, which isn't necessarily bad, but it IS when Eminem is at a bigger level than he was in 1998. "When the Music Stops" featuring the not-so-great rappers, D12, is a flat out filler cut. The ONLY filler cut on this album. Nothing against Bizarre from D12, but c'mon, even a mute person raps better than this guy. He doesn't even attempt to rap. He just talks slowly. Think he earned his recording contract? I don't think so. You think if Eminem weren't in the rap game this guy would never EVER get a recording contract? I think so. And what's with Proof always whispering? Use your regular voice for God's sake!
Even though this LP has a couple of OK songs, even those can grow on you. Not only is this CD good, it's great. Eminem is arguably hip-hop's top rapper, the only other rapper contending for the title would be Jay-Z. A "Renegade Part 2" would have been awesome on here. Eminem has the potential to be one of hip-hop's top leading producers also as he produced all but three songs on this disc. The sad thing is, there might be a day when Slim does not need Dr. Dre anymore. The way things are going, when Eminems contract is up, he will record on his own label, Shady Records. I'm sure Dre will still hook him up with beats. Marshall has grown A LOT since he came in the rap game. His lashes against his own mother alone is unique in the music business. Most rappers praise their moms instead of berating them. Jay-Z, Tupac, Notorious B.I.G., Snoop Dogg, Warren G, and a few other rappers "love their mommas." Em also disses his dad whom left Marshall's life when he was a baby. Now this is more common amongst rappers. WC and the Madd Circle, Beanie Sigel, 2pac, and more have all laid out their frustrations against their fathers. The Eminem Show will most likely be the top selling cd of the year. Not only because it's filled with shock value tagged along with controversy, but because Marshall Mathers is arguably the hardest working lyricist in hip-hop. One can not listen to this album and deny this young man's talent. Two other things are very, very, obvious upon listening to this LP: His unconditional ever-lasting love for the person he treasures the most in the world, little Hailie Jade Mathers, and how big of an inspiration the late, great, Tupac Shakur is in Em's life. I counted about five 2pac references in this cd. There might be more. Slim Shady does not give a you know what whether you like him or not. All he wants is your respect. And damn it, he deserves it, and guess what? He most certainly is going to get it whether you want to give it to him or not. Mrs. Mathers' baby boy wouldn't want it any other way.

It's a challenge to parents everywhere to ask "Do we just not like his lyrics, or are we ticked that are kid are relating to his lyrics?".
But through it all, Eminem retains his bratty wit, mocking all the usual suspects, (he's got a real grip with Tipper Gore and the Cheyney family) and, though I sometimes question his logic, it's still a hoot. Eminem has always been about not caring about anything and just trying to cause controversey. Well, he's still going to be causing controversey, but he definitely shows weakness in this album. He shows hate, anger, and love in this very powerful album. If you're expecting the same old Eminem, you've got another thing coming. Let's get to the song reviews.
White America - A-: This is a great song, it's a pillar to the fact that America still doesn't get it. He's letting all the parents know he was out to prove to the world how many parents out there just aren't parents.
Business - C-: The album quickly hits a low point with this song, this is one of the many songs that make you feel like being tortured by having to sit through it. Eminem has good lyrics, but as long as he's not saying anything, this one just gets lame.
Cleaning Out My Closet - A++: This is probably the strongest song he's ever done. It's a message to all about the true situation with his mom. A very powerful song. He shows one weakness right here... his hate for his parents.
Square Dance - B-: Another song taking a jab at those that criticize him. There are quite a lot of these.
Soldier - B+: This is honestly a song that can scare you under the right circumstances. Eminem has a lot of anger over losing his ex-wife, Kim, and in this song, he really displays that.
Say Goodbye To Hollywood - C+: Can't figure this one out myself. It's alright... not the best he's done though. Wait, he hates hollywood... hell, what celebrity doesn't?
Drips - D-: I'm sorry, there's no reason for this song to exist. It's lame.
Without Me - A-: A throwback to the true Eminem we've come to know. Though, if you think about it, this guy is a true schizo. There's Slim Shady, Marshall Mathers, and Eminem. Pick your favorite flavor!
Sing For The Moment - B+: Eminem's version of the hit by Aerosmith, Dream On. I honestly enjoy this song a lot. I don't know what it is, but he's able to always sound so passionate about everything.
Superman - C+: This is kind of a weird song, cause it makes no real sense. I guess he's just still angry with women after Kim.
Hailie's Song - B-: This song really shows his love for his daughter... another weakness of his. Possibly though, seeing these weaknesses will bring a more artistic and human feel to his work. I'm honestly liking this side of Mr. Mathers.
When The Music Stops - F: The only really bad song on this album. It's just a boring one, and you'll most likely skip it.
Say What You Say - F+: I can't get into his songs that he writes for rappers he hates. Jermaine Dupri is really horrible, but not worth a song.
'Till I Collapse - A: I feel the desperation of this song. He conveys emotion so well.
My Dad's Gone Crazy - B+: This is honestly quite funny. He gets his daughter on the track, and it's really cute and disturbing at the same time... and that's why I like it.
So, in coclusion, buy it. Eminem really does get much better with each album. Of course, he also gets a bit more twisted each album too... he's an artist, what do you want? It's the same way Jonathan Davis sounds a bit more sucidal with each CD. Artist just exploit their demons for money... which is a wonderful way to deal with it, in my opinion. At least he's not out there shooting people.

"The Eminem Show" displays a maturing Marshall Bruce Mathers III in an album that's not as funny as "The Slim Shady LP" or as shocking as "The Marshall Mathers LP". The title is a takeoff of the Jim Carrey movie "The Truman Show". Thus we get a brutally real view of his adult life, kind of where "Slim Shady" left off. By now there's no question of his rap skills; he's easily the most talented and original MC working right now. Although most of this album is serious, there's still some funny moments, offensive lyrics, and the usual lot of disses (Lynn Chaney, Tipper Gore, the Bush administration, Chris Kirkpatrick, Moby, Jermaine Dupri, his mom and dad) and loves (Dr. Dre, his fans, the rap business, and especially his daughter Hailie). But the bulk of this album is Em's life and the world around him. That, along with the incredible beats and rhyming skills make this his best album so far, in my opinion. Standout tracks include:WHITE AMERICA-Em's view on how the fact that he's white helped make him the star he is today and how some members of the government were attempting to violate his right to free speech.  He also takes time out to thank Dr. Dre for launching his career.  BUSINESS-A clever Batman-themed rant from Em and Dre about how important they are to the rap industry. CLEANING OUT MY CLOSET-Easily my favorite on this album. This displays the multi-dimensional Em I've been looking for. It's a showdown with his mother Debbie. He does admit to some wrongdoing, then he lashes out at her faults. He even mentions that "Set The Record Straight" CD she put out in 2000. This certainly isn't the typical mother/son relationship that most of us have been blessed with. The last line of this song will show once and for all why Em disrespects her. This track is featured in his upcoming movie "8 Mile". SAYIN' GOODBYE TO HOLLYWOOD-More confessional from Em, this time on his divorce from Kim and how his rage over her extramarrital affair neary pushed him over the edge, but didn't because of his devotion to his daughter.  As much as I despised that "Kim" track on "Marshall Mathers", it's certainly better to rap about murdering your wife than to do it. WITHOUT ME-This fun, funny, radio-friendly first single is Em mocking his own controversial image and how the fans eat it up. ("I've created a monster, 'cuz nobody wants to see Marshall no more. They want Shady. I'm chopped liver.") HALIE'S SONG-A loving ode to his daughter. He sings (sort of)! WHEN THE MUSIC STOPS-A funny commentary by Em and the rest of his dirty half-dozen on how music and reality can be blurred. The funniest and most tragic editorial comes from Bizarre. MY DAD'S GONE CRAZY-Now we hear Hailie's cute voice, introducing her dad as he slams the goverment and his Mom some more. Of course, some of Em's views will make you cringe, especially his view on govenment which won't sit well with our war on terrorism (It's a good thing this album got released 8 1/2 months after 9/11). And a couple of tracks didn't quite work. DRIPS could've been a clever cautionary tale against unprotected sex but the lyrics were too graphic. And SING FOR THE MOMENT, a commentary on why rappers express themselves so explicitly, shamelessly rips off Aerosmith's "Dream On". (C'mon, Em, you're too talented to resort to sampling) But Em's raw honesty makes for a very compelling CD.  The DVD is basically a promotional sampler with excerpts from his "E" and "The Slim Shady Show" and his upcoming "All Access Europe" DVD's, and a trailer for his upcoming movie "8 Mile".  It does have some rare concert footage and interviews.  (He's begging us to buy his D-12 album, since it didn't sell nearly as well as first 2 albums did, or as well as this one will).

The is album is definitley some of Eminem's best work, he is obviously maturing as a MC. He is finally past making fun of pop-related bands, and moved to some more serious issues. Dolly Parton once said that "The hardest thing for a performer to demonstrate is sincerity. Once you can fake that, you've got it made." Eminem would like us to think he's highly sincere, with his unending self-gratification, but with this third (or fourth, if you count the labored D-12 disc) CD he begins to come across as self-aware. He's the hero of suburban kids everywhere he proclaims in "White America". He's a ticking time-bomb in "Soldier" and "My Dad's Gone Crazy". He's a dedicated father in "Hallie's Song". He's this, he's that, he's the other and then he's back again. At what point does all this superego hopscotch become valid and at what point does it become the Eminmen Copyrighted Selling Point, that he can summon at will, and will continue to do so for as long as it makes a buck? I ask this because even as you're bobbing your head to the relentless beats conjured by Em and Dre, you'll still be getting the sense of deja vu. It really is the Eminem Show with Em, Mom, Kim, Hallie, Dre, and the nutty cast of characters popping in and out. He's as vocally dexterous as ever, (we could spend all day reciting the witty and memorable lines displayed in just a few songs.) and as I stated, songs like "Square Dance" and of course "Without Me" are guaranteed car-radio hits.
It's just this: even hit sitcoms run out of new ideas, and Em is well on his way there; after he gets through ragging on family members, he contrives enemies out of thin air, (MTV tried to shut him down? The Source doesn't respect him?) Worst of all, he's starting to indulge in vulgarity for vulgarity's sake like Too Short or 2 Live Crew with the ultra-misogynistic "Drip" and "Superman"; it's not just that these tracks are disgusting, it's that after staking his claim as the ultimate individual, such pandering like this should be beneath him. Those quibbles aside, it's another fun filled hour with MM, and he'll undoubtedly be renewed next season, even if the ratings start to shudder.

Eminem will always keep himself on the public's mind by using extreme and shocking subject matter in his songs, but decades from now, his undeniable talent will keep his name alive.
  His third full-length CD, The Eminem Show, hits the stores of a much different America than before, when both The Slim Shady LP and The Marshall Mathers LP brought him critical and commercial success. The rapper has obviously become more reclusive and contemplative, and it comes through in the new songs so clearly and intelligently that the shock appeal actually loses its front seat status.
  If his last set proved worthy of an album of the year Grammy nomination, Show deserves to win the award. Not only does Eminem continue to address critics, the government, and personal enemies with well-thought-out insults and lyrical poison, he attacks himself with just as much venom.
  His messages far from one-sided, he talks tough but true about his past actions and regrets. From first track to last, the album works as a verbalization of a poet's overworked mind, and the beats ain't bad either.
  The first half of Show builds on past controversy and content, such as Eminem's ongoing struggle with his mother ("Cleanin Out My Closet") and his alleged assault on a man kissing his wife outside a club ("Say Goodbye Hollywood"). While cynics and critics might feel inclined to shout, "who cares?" at these subjects, Eminem knows his fans want to hear his thoughts about them. Some of the most well respected literature in the world tackles biographical subjects, so what's different about rap music?
  Halfway through the CD, the songs have put a unique and refreshing perspective on everything from the artist's life to the War on Terrorism, and one begins to wonder how the songs can build or progress anymore than they already have. Well, after track No. 10, the CD's first single "Without Me," ends, Mathers moves into a breathtaking seven-song opus that would impress even the most jaded rap haters.
  Most relevant artists have one song in their careers that fully identifies their reason for being, and "Sing for the Moment" does that for Eminem. Using purposeful samples from the underrated Aerosmith classic "Dream On," each verse beautifully portrays a different facet or motivation of the rapper's career, and it ends with a message that explains the appeal of rap music better than anything ever has.
  Another risky but unforgettable move comes in "Hailie's Song," where Eminem drops any remains of his tough exterior and actually sings about his daughter's effect on his life. Complete with recorded harmonies and soft vocal stylings, he transforms himself into something much more real than any microphone `gangsta' or sex-obsessed hustler.
  Any reasonable person, including the rapper himself, would say The Eminem Show isn't for children, who would have trouble getting past the profanity and adult themes to fully recognize the messages. But adults who love both rap and literature will see the merit and meaning in this record.
  Whether the lyrics get the same amount of protest and attention they have gotten before, the artistry of Eminem will only make a positive mark on rap and all other forms of music.

These are great containers. At first, I was very disappointed in how poorly of a fit the lid and container were. But I decided to try them anyway, and proceeded to sanitize them properly.

Being a chef for six years has taught me many things. One of which, you should always boil new plastic containers for at least a minute (best at 5 minutes) to remove any contaminants from manufacturing. We get enough plastics and other chemicals in our diets already. And if you are buying for your kid's lunches like I did, you should do this purely for your family's sake.

The trick to plastic containers with fitted lids is that after you boil them in plain tap water for at least one minute:
1. Remove from boiling water using a pair of tongs or a slotted spoon.
2. Tip the container/lid so most of the water drains back into the pot.
3. Immediately find it's matching container/lid from the pot, and after draining it as well, put the two pieces together.
4. Allow to cool.
5. The lid and container should now be a much better fit. They might still be snug, but should be much easier on your fingers.

Don't take my word for it though. Please only try one at first to make sure it works as well for you as it does for me.

Product Usefulness - 5 stars I bought these containers to use as portable salt and pepper shakers. My plan was to carry them back and forth between work and home (on public transportation) so I needed something that would be small, light, and unbreakable. I had tried the Tupperware Midget Salt & Pepper Shaker NEW Rare Purple, but found that the 2-ounce size of the container was too big, and that it took up too much room at the office and in my tote bag. This smaller, 1-ounce size was much better for meeting my needs. Luckily, Tupperware makes their products so that the same size lids will sometimes work on similar containers, depending on the size of the lip of the container. These two products looked like the lids would be interchangeable, so I took a chance and placed the order. I'm happy to report the shaker part of the original set I bought fits perfectly onto this container. By the way, the salt and pepper lids work on this set, too: Tupperware Smidget Container 1oz Each Assorted Set 5 I have been hunting for a good set of portable salt and pepper shakers for years. By combining these two products, the mission was accomplished! Note - I plan to re-post this review, with minor variations, on these two other product pages, so if you see it over there, you won't need to re-read the details. Any Tupperware container with a round lid is leak proof, so you can fill them up with small quantities of shampoo, conditioner, mouthwash, toothpaste, etc., and take them on the road, without worrying about leaks. I have NEVER had a problem with a leak from a Tupperware container with a round lip. As an added bonus, the containers have a lot of uses. You can use them to keep your spices fresh. My mom used to use them to store Wilton icing coloring dyes. They would be good for small quantities of craft products. They are perfect for maintaining order over the small things that get thrown into a junk drawer. These things are handy, so this list could go on and on. From my experience with Tupperware, sometimes the lids are a bit tight-fitting when they are new. If you soak the lid in hot water for a couple of minutes, it will expand slightly, and will easily fit onto the container. You should only need to do this one or two times; after that, they should fit without pre-soaking. Color - 2 stars The color is ugly, and I would not call it pink. It is more of a watered-down version of a coral-like (or maybe salmon-like) tint than pink. When I saw the color on the computer screen, I thought the color difference between my idea of pink and the reality would be chalked up to the virtual world. But the reality was worse than the monitor. :p Saying this color is "pink" isn't even as accurate as saying that "aquamarine" is "green" or "blue." I'm glad I didn't plan to keep these out on the table. Value Analysis - 3 stars In the past, it was always been worth paying a little extra for Tupperware because of the superior quality of the Tupperware brand, as well as the lifetime guarantee. With this order, however, I noticed that the plastic feels slightly thinner and more brittle than the Tupperware containers I bought 20 years ago. I actually took some of the older containers out and did a side-by-side comparison, and I liked the older ones better. I'm afraid the containers may not be as durable as they used to be, but they still seem to be very durable. Tupperware is still superior to most plastics, but the quality of Rubbermaid has improved over the years, and Rubbermaid is much less expensive. If my Rubbermaid fails, I just throw it out and buy a new one. When I have used the warranty, it has provided a needed replacement for a favorite piece of plastic, and I've been very pleased with the results. Balance this against the fact that, if I want to return a Tupperware product that fails, I have to pay shipping to send it back to them. This is often just as expensive as the cost of the item being replaced. I also have to pay shipping and handling for them to send the replacement back to me. According to their web site, this is currently (May 2013) a flat rate of $5.75. (And this assumes that the item can still be replaced, and you don't end up with a substitute. You may wind up with a replacement of a different color, so the set you have no longer matches.) I have a few pieces of Tupperware that need to be replaced, but have decided it's just not economical to do so. So the pieces sit there in the back of the closet while I wait for the pile to grow large enough to make it worth the cost of sending them in and getting them replaced. I have tried to convince myself to just throw them out, but they don't take up much room. ;) Is Tupperware worth the extra cost? Yes, but only for especially useful and/or unique pieces. Personally, I'm planning to seek out this brand only if nothing else will meet the need I have.

Being a chef for six years has taught me many things. One of which, you should always boil new plastic containers for at least a minute (best at 5 minutes) to remove any contaminants from manufacturing. We get enough plastics and other chemicals in our diets already. And if you are buying for your kid's lunches like I did, you should do this purely for your family's sake.

The trick to plastic containers with fitted lids is that after you boil them in plain tap water for at least one minute:
1. Remove from boiling water using a pair of tongs or a slotted spoon.
2. Tip the container/lid so most of the water drains back into the pot.
3. Immediately find it's matching container/lid from the pot, and after draining it as well, put the two pieces together.
4. Allow to cool.
5. The lid and container should now be a much better fit. They might still be snug, but should be much easier on your fingers.

Don't take my word for it though. Please only try one at first to make sure it works as well for you as it does for me.

I purchased a Lasko 5160 to provide electric heat in our 32' travel trailer while connected to shore power in Spokane, WA in winter.  Works great to heat the trailer - temp got down to 15 degrees one night, and we never had to use propane heat (although I DID have to adjust the trailer's thermostat down to 65 to prevent the gas heat from coming on.)

I like the quiet oscillating feature, good heat projection/distribution, and the fact that the (plastic!) grill on the front of the heater doesn't get very warm at all, but there are a few things I DON'T like:

1) The thermostatic (Auto) function only works on "Hi", so the heater draws the full 1500 watts when it is set to Auto.  I had to add a dedicated 15 amp GFCI outlet for the heater because all existing outlets in our trailer are on one GFCI because you can't set this heater to Auto + low power. Needless to say, we have to do a lot of "power management" with the heater turned on Auto, because running a coffeemaker, microwave, etc. in conjunction with the heater's 1500 watt load can trip the trailer's 30 amp main breaker.  Not usually - but it does happen.

2) When power to the heater is disconnected or the heater is turned off, when power is turned on again, the heater remains off, and it doesn't "remember" the fact that it was "on", that it was set to Auto, or that it was set to oscillate.

3) There is no indicator for the "oscillate" function - you get left to guess if the fan is set to oscillate, or it just isn't oscillating because the Auto function is being used and the room temperature is warm enough to trip the thermostat to "off".

The Lasko 5160 is a good buy, but it would be "great" buy if Lasko would address these issues.

These are great containers. At first, I was very disappointed in how poorly of a fit the lid and container were. But I decided to try them anyway, and proceeded to sanitize them properly.

Being a chef for six years has taught me many things. One of which, you should always boil new plastic containers for at least a minute (best at 5 minutes) to remove any contaminants from manufacturing. We get enough plastics and other chemicals in our diets already. And if you are buying for your kid's lunches like I did, you should do this purely for your family's sake.

The trick to plastic containers with fitted lids is that after you boil them in plain tap water for at least one minute:
1. Remove from boiling water using a pair of tongs or a slotted spoon.
2. Tip the container/lid so most of the water drains back into the pot.
3. Immediately find it's matching container/lid from the pot, and after draining it as well, put the two pieces together.
4. Allow to cool.
5. The lid and container should now be a much better fit. They might still be snug, but should be much easier on your fingers.

Don't take my word for it though. Please only try one at first to make sure it works as well for you as it does for me.

These are great containers. At first, I was very disappointed in how poorly of a fit the lid and container were. But I decided to try them anyway, and proceeded to sanitize them properly.

Being a chef for six years has taught me many things. One of which, you should always boil new plastic containers for at least a minute (best at 5 minutes) to remove any contaminants from manufacturing. We get enough plastics and other chemicals in our diets already. And if you are buying for your kid's lunches like I did, you should do this purely for your family's sake.

The trick to plastic containers with fitted lids is that after you boil them in plain tap water for at least one minute:
1. Remove from boiling water using a pair of tongs or a slotted spoon.
2. Tip the container/lid so most of the water drains back into the pot.
3. Immediately find it's matching container/lid from the pot, and after draining it as well, put the two pieces together.
4. Allow to cool.
5. The lid and container should now be a much better fit. They might still be snug, but should be much easier on your fingers.

Don't take my word for it though. Please only try one at first to make sure it works as well for you as it does for me.

I hope this helps everyone purchasing this product.

They need to be screwed into something secure, not just drywall. There's going to be significant pull on the bases, and you don't want your curtains sagging! Hit a stud- usually about 1/2 inch out from the window edge. Mount the bases, then snap the covers over them. Mount them both first. Then extend the mechanism on the right side as far as it'll go. The instructions show how to do this, but it's easy even if you don't have instructions. There are 3 cylinders on the right side. The left one holds the wire, the right one is attached to the wall, and the center one connects them and tightens the wire once it's attached. The right piece isn't moving. It's screwed to the wall. Use the supplied Allen wrench to loosen the tiny nuts on the left fixture. Insert the wire. Tighten the tiny nuts onto the wire.  Stretch the wire until it'll fit into the right fixture with no slack. Having a friend helps here, but isn't necessary. Loosen the nuts on the right side, insert the wire, and tighten the tiny nuts again. Now hold the left cylinder so it doesn't turn, and turn the middle cylinder to take up the slack! Seriously- they sometimes don't come with instructions. The "wire" is actually a thin, braided cable, so wire cutters are necessary to keep the ends from fraying. Frayed cable won't want to go into the holes. Don't be afraid of the installation process- it's a snap.

Ok, the instructions are garbage, but then again, it is Ikea. For the right bracket, there are three components. To eliminate sag, extend the far left piece with two holes (first piece) all the way and then extend the middle piece with one hole (second piece) all the way as well. This is critical. I used 16 gauge steel galvanized wire instead of what was supplied as it gets frayed. Measure the wire to fit all the way into the back of the first piece and then cut with good wire cutters. Secure it with the two tiny nuts. Insert the Allen wrench into the one hole within the second piece, keep your right hand on the wall bracket (third piece) to prevent it from turning and begin turning towards you (clockwise motion). I told my girlfriend that I'd write this because I spent more time than I care to admit trying to figure out that BOTH the first and second pieces need to be fully extended when you begin to tighten. I'd also recommend using the clamps (sold separately) than the eyelets because you can take them down easier to clean. Also recommend having them professionally hemmed to avoid the flimsy hem tape coming out in the washer/dryer. - Mike

I just installed this today for a room divider in a small room. I used about 9ft of the wire that came with the kit and I have several feet left. The description states that you need to supply your own fasteners/hardware, so unless this addition was just made to the item description, no one can complain about this. I bought some #12 1 1/2" wood screws so that the heads fit into the pre-countersunk holes in the metal plates that you attach to the walls. One plate and three screws went into a stud and the other into a very smooth masonry wall with some Gorilla Glue. This Gorilla Glue works in *my* case - I must have put about 15 lbs of downward pressure on it and for *me* it was fine, especially since less than 3 pounds will be hanging from it. I hate drilling through masonry walls in a rented house, and so this alternative works fine for me. The fact that the installation instructions are all pictorial was not a problem, the assembly was easy. If you're used to putting things together yourself, this is a simple project. The hardest thing is positiong the wire plates at either wall exactly where you want them if no studs are present. I don't want the wire to sag, so I checked for stud locations *before* ordering this, knowing that I might also have to use masonry anchors and screws. If you can't attach this to wall studs, you might just want to go with ceiling curtain rod brackets ad a very lightweight curtain rod (all of which Ikea happens to have for a lot, lot less than Home Depot).

If you want to be really cheap, twist two screw eye hooks into the wall studs (I hope they're directly opposite one another) and get some wire. But I do like the simple tension system with this set. The 17mm spacing they indicate you should use is good, especially if you're doing a long room and the wire tends to sag more during installation. With my 9ft room, I only needed about 10mm because my cut wire length was fairly tight to start. Better to cut off too little than too much - you can always cut more off later.

A cordless screwdriver/drill and cutting pliers may be needed if you don't already have them.

When I was visiting my local Ikea store, I saw their use of this curtain wire set for the first time and I loved it. I have been looking for a way to display pics of my grandkids because the refrigerator is already maxxed out with magnets and photos. I saw great possibilities with this curtain-hanging set, so I bought it.

Somewhere on the package it reads, "Easy to cut." No way. It is difficult. The wire itself is made of many smaller wires rolled together, just like a basket handle or a rope.  The first three sets of wire cutters I tried did not do the job. At first I thought it wouldn't make any difference if the wires at the ends of the "rope" were separated -- thought I could twist them back together again, but I couldn't. I couldn't crimp them together, couldn't twist them together, so the "rope" would not insert into the tiny hole of the bracket. I had to recut the edges with great patience, cutting each single wire one at a time, twisting the "rope" gently so that the wires would not unravel or mangel.

Once that was done, the ends of the "rope" did fit into the small holes of the bracket. However, despite how I pulled the "rope" to tighten the slack, I just couldn't level it out. I tightened and untightened screws, and finally, after a couple hours of all this, I just gave up. After all, I told myself, this is only for a photo display.  However, the length of my entire display is only 28". One could only wonder what would happen if you had to actually hang draperies from this wire set; seems to me that the slack would be awful.

The next day, I took the remaining wire "rope" to work to ask the head of maintenance to trim off the edges so that I could use it for a picture display in my office. He used two different sets of professional wire cutters with great difficulty, but finally managed to cut the "rope." At least it didn't take him the hours it took me!

That being said, I love the over-all look of my photo display; it will be very easy to change photos and artwork.

Since I am not using this wire set for draperies, but rather for photos, I give the set 4 stars; I am subtracting a star for the hours it took me to cut the rope correctly.  There is a less-expensive version of this from Ikea, and if I had it to do over again, I would buy that one.

I've had a pile of this hardware for several years, given it heavy use in a variety of applications, and it still looks and functions like brand new. The only trouble is it's pretty tricky to install. I've never been able to figure it out and have had to rely on the kindness of boyfriends to do it for me (really, IKEA, would it be that hard to put WORDS with your picture-instructions?!?). One time I lived in an old building with plaster walls rather than drywall, and the plaster stuck to the wall-mounts like crazy when I took it down. If you have plaster walls, be prepared to repair damage if/when you uninstall this hardware. (Also, the stuck-on plaster was impossible to remove from the wall-mounts until I figured out the solution: put it in boiling water for a few minutes!). The wire is rather difficult to cut, and I've had to purchase new wire when I've needed it to be longer than what I have left. Overall it's a great product, especially if you don't plan on having to install it more than once!

(Oh, and to the people complaining about having to buy screws separately: really?!? Different types of walls will require different types of screws, and you're whining about something that costs nearly nothing and is available practically everywhere).
